[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
A Korean travel packing checklist card for a suitcase, designed as a realistic printable vertical organizer sheet and photographed like premium stationery. The image should feel useful for actual trip preparation: category-based packing, handwritten checking, destination notes, travel dates, luggage weight notes, and small editorial travel-planner details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the main checklist board as a portrait A4-style card, filling most of the canvas while leaving a visible paper edge and print-safe trim area.
- Use a polished travel-planner page structure: large Korean title at top, compact metadata strip, category blocks stacked vertically, and {체크박스 형식} aligned beside every item.
- Background should feel like premium warm off-white paper with tangible grain, slight page thickness, faint fold impression, tiny ink registration marks, and realistic printed texture.
- Add natural travel-stationery context around the card: a corner of a baggage tag, a boarding-pass strip, small route-map line art, a capped pen, subtle masking tape tabs, and tiny packing stickers, all kept secondary to the checklist.
- Keep the framing flat and orthographic so the card remains printable, with {여행 종류} and {카테고리 짐} driving the content hierarchy.
- {체크박스 형식} must be visible beside each packing item, evenly spaced for manual ticking, with a few sample handwritten-looking tick marks in amber on nonessential demo rows only.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone top 12–15%: place the title as a strong Korean masthead, followed by a smaller subtitle that reflects {여행 종류}. Include realistic planner labels such as PACKING LIST VOL.12, 2026.05, 여행 준비 체크 01, and a small model-style credit line: Card design by @travel_note.
2. Trip information strip beneath header: create labeled fields in Korean for 여행지, 출발일, 귀국일, 동행, 예상 날씨, 캐리어 무게, and 비상연락. Use dotted writing lines and small icons such as airplane, suitcase, cloud, plug, pill, and passport.
3. Main checklist grid middle 65–70%: divide into clear category cards or boxed sections for each group in {카테고리 짐}, each section with item rows, prices or quantities where natural, and left-aligned checkboxes.
4. Visual support area: use {시각화} as the central organizing motif, rendered as a practical travel editorial infographic: suitcase flat layout, folded clothes, toiletries pouch, charger cable, passport, medication pouch, and small travel accessories represented as neat illustrated modules.
5. Checklist rows: each line should be short, highly legible, and spaced for handwriting; include {체크박스 형식} with consistent alignment and padding. Add realistic rows such as 티셔츠 3장, 속옷 4개, 양말 4켤레, 세면도구, 선크림, 보조배터리, 충전기, 여권·신분증, 상비약, 우산, 목베개.
6. Footer zone: include a compact reminder box with 출발 전 확인, page indicator 01/01, small QR-style decorative block, barcode-like baggage label area, and a CTA line: 떠나기 전 3분 체크.
7. Color guidance: apply {컬러 톤} across section headers, divider lines, check marks, micro icons, stickers, and route-map accents while keeping the cream paper base dominant.
8. Format treatment: maintain {비율} as a portrait print card with all text visible, realistic print bleed, tidy hierarchy, and editorial balance.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold for the main title, Pretendard SemiBold for category labels, and Noto Sans KR Regular for checklist lines; title size should feel like 34–44px equivalent, body text 18–22px equivalent, metadata text 10–14px equivalent.
- Color palette: cream #F4EBDD, charcoal #2F2F2F, warm amber #C98A3A, soft beige #DCCFBF, muted brown-gray #7C6E62.
- Border/shadow: thin 1.5px charcoal rules, rounded section boxes, dotted writing lines, small amber tabs, very soft paper shadow with 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity.
- Add tactile printed details: tiny ink speckles, slightly imperfect stamped labels, warm toner texture, faint paper fibers, sticker edges, and small hand-drawn travel icons.
- Decorative elements should support packing usability: section dividers, baggage-tag label, route arrows, tiny page markers, and check reminder badges.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat lay aesthetic, simulated as a clean studio document photo shot on a 50mm lens at f/5.6 for even geometry and low distortion.
- Lighting: diffused softbox from upper-left at 45° with faint fill from lower-right, creating gentle paper depth, realistic contact shadows from the pen, tape, baggage tag, and card edge.
- Color grade: warm cream + charcoal + amber with slightly muted travel-magazine tonality, like a high-end stationery spread photographed for a planner catalog.
- Material rendering: matte paper, lightly textured ink, soft fabric-like tape, semi-matte pen plastic, and slightly glossy boarding-pass strip.

[6. MOOD]
Practical travel magazine checklist page — feels like a Kinfolk-style editorial planner mixed with a clean Japanese stationery catalog layout, but more lived-in and ready for real packing.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: 여행 캐리어 짐정리 카드, 2박 3일 국내 — 또는 7일 해외·비즈니스·캠핑·신혼여행, 옷 (티셔츠 3 / 속옷 4 / 양말 4) / 화장품 / 전자기기 / 약·서류 / 여행소품, 캐리어 안 펼친 평면 뷰 또는 옷·소품 일러스트 콜라주, 카테고리별 박스, 각 짐 옆 작은 체크박스 □ — 인쇄해서 직접 체크 가능, 크림 + 차콜 + 따뜻한 amber — 여행 매거진 결, A4 세로 1024x1536.
- Additional Korean microcopy should be crisp and readable: PACKING LIST VOL.12, 2026.05, 여행 준비 체크 01, 여행지, 출발일, 귀국일, 동행, 예상 날씨, 캐리어 무게, 비상연락, 출발 전 확인, 떠나기 전 3분 체크, Page 01/01, @travel_note.
- All Korean characters must be crisp and correctly rendered, with no broken glyphs.
- Checklist rows must remain clean, aligned, realistic, and suitable for manual ticking.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Unauthorized celebrity likeness or celebrity composites

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean airline ticket and boarding pass mockup, Instagram-shareable travel brag graphic with premium editorial realism.
Single hero composition that feels like a polished airline document flat lay, combining ticketing details, scannable travel graphics, baggage cues, and luxury travel accessories.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main ticket / boarding pass card occupies about 72% of the frame, placed slightly right of center with a second overlapping pass at 18° angle for depth.
- {항공사·노선} appears as the primary ticket line in the upper section, with {탑승 정보} placed in the mid-lower data block and {승객 정보} as the passenger name field.
- Add realistic airline-document details: {터미널·탑승구}, {예약·발권번호}, {수하물·등급}, {가격·결제}, a QR code, vertical barcode, perforated tear-off stub, boarding group badge, seat map mini icon, and small itinerary captions.
- Background uses {배경} arranged as a styled flat-lay on an off-white tabletop, with subtle paper grain, passport edges, luggage tag string, coffee sleeve texture, and a faint shadowed edge around each object.
- {브랜드 시그니처} is reflected in the accent stripe, header band, route marker, baggage tag, and micro UI details; include a small airline-style wordmark area and realistic document numbering.
- {컬러 톤} controls the overall palette across ticket paper, tabletop, props, barcode ink, printed rules, and editorial shadows.
- Framing should feel like a high-end social media product shot, with all Korean and English text crisp, aligned, and easy to read in a square feed crop.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero ticket block: place the main boarding pass front and center, sized to dominate the composition, with sharp rectangular edges, realistic matte laminated paper texture, perforation dots, and a detachable right-side stub.
2. Secondary layer: offset a second ticket behind the first, partially visible on the left or top edge, showing repeated route code, baggage tag number, and a cropped barcode to create a stacked travel-document effect.
3. Information hierarchy: render {항공사·노선} in the top header area, {탑승 정보} in the central data zone, {승객 정보} as a bold name line near the bottom, and {터미널·탑승구} as a prominent capsule label beside the seat field.
4. Document realism: include {예약·발권번호} near the barcode, {수하물·등급} in a small data table, {가격·결제} on a receipt-like strip, and tiny labels such as 탑승순서, 출발터미널, 예약번호, 발권일, 여정구분.
5. Travel props: arrange {배경} around the ticket with a passport corner, leather luggage tag, folded receipt, pen, boarding sleeve, coffee cup rim, and fabric handle texture, with the ticket remaining the unmistakable focal object.
6. Color balance: use {컬러 톤} across background, accents, paper stock, object shadows, and printed ink so the mockup feels cohesive and magazine-like instead of generic.
7. Social-detail layer: add {여행캡션} as a small handwritten-style note card or sticker near the bottom edge, plus {날짜·위치라벨} as a compact editorial label in the corner.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard and Noto Sans KR for Korean UI text, with a clean airline-style sans serif in medium to bold weights; header at 28–34 px equivalent, details at 16–20 px equivalent, small labels at 11–13 px equivalent.
- Color palette: derive from {컬러 톤}; use a cream base (#F6F1E8 or similar), deep airline navy, white ticket fields, charcoal secondary text, pale blue data cells, and one warm accent for tags or stickers.
- Border/shadow: soft drop shadow with 4px y-offset, 14px blur, 18% opacity; thin 1px rules; slightly rounded corners only if consistent with the ticket design; add perforation dots and small printed crop marks for realism.
- Surface finish: matte paper with subtle fiber texture, faint print registration feel, crisp vector-like UI edges, barcode ink density variation, and gentle wear on ticket corners.
- Decorative graphics: use route arrows, airport-code circles, small airplane pictograms, baggage icons, calendar chips, and ticket-stub dividers as functional document decoration.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 85mm f/2.8 product photography look, slightly elevated front-facing angle, compressed perspective for a premium mockup presentation.
- Lighting: soft studio key from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from right, controlled shadow falloff beneath the stacked tickets and props.
- Color grade: cream highlights, navy accents, charcoal text, with mild contrast and clean editorial saturation similar to a luxury travel magazine flat lay.

[6. MOOD]
Premium travel editorial — feel of a Kinfolk x Monocle-style journey spread with refined airline document realism, subtle anticipation before departure, and polished first-class travel brag energy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: must render these strings exactly as intended in the mockup: "대한항공 KE 705 — 인천(ICN) → 도쿄 나리타(NRT)", "2026.06.15 (월) 09:25 → 11:50 / 게이트 32 / 좌석 18A", "HONG GILDONG · 일등석 또는 비즈니스 — 자유 자랑 결", "대한항공 시그니처 (다크 블루 + 화이트) — 또는 아시아나·제주·진에어 등", "여행 가방 + 여권 + 커피 정물 — 또는 단일 hero 컷", "크림 + 항공사 시그니처 + 차콜 — 매거진 결", "1024x1024 정사각".
- Also render these added travel-document strings clearly: "터미널 2 · 탑승구 32 · BOARDING ZONE A", "예약번호 PNR-7K2Q9 · 발권번호 180-2567894321", "위탁수하물 2PC · 비즈니스 플렉스", "항공권 ₩1,248,000 · 카드 결제 완료", "떠나요, 월요일 아침의 도쿄", "2026.06.15 · 인천국제공항".
- Text must be sharply aligned, fully legible, and preserve exact Korean punctuation, airport-code capitalization, numbers, arrows, and spacing.
- Keep the ticket mockup composition centered and layered; the primary ticket must remain the dominant focal object with barcode, QR code, stub, and route details readable.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications / immigration stamps
- Broken Korean characters
- Actual photographed celebrity or passenger likenesses

[1. PURPOSE]
Digital passport stamp and travel sticker collectible collage, designed like an Instagram-worthy travel souvenir sheet and photographed as a tangible scrapbook page.
Vertical poster-format layout with a playful, organized passport-stamp archive aesthetic, enriched with realistic collector-sheet details, travel labels, date marks, serial text, tape pieces, and souvenir ephemera.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main composition: a centered travel collage occupying about 85% of the frame, with {레이아웃} controlling whether the stickers sit in a lively freeform cluster or a structured collectible grid.
- Background treatment: {배경} with tactile paper grain, slightly worn fibers, tiny scuffs, faint crease marks, scanned-document shadows, and warm travel-journal texture.
- Header area: include a bold Korean title block reading "디지털 여권 도장·여행 스티커", plus small metadata such as "COLLECTOR SHEET", "VOL.024", "2026.05", "PAGE 01", and "@travel.archive".
- Subject distribution: {방문 국가들} should be separated into individual stamp units and sticker-ticket fragments, each country treated like a collected arrival mark with its own small date, route code, and caption label.
- Souvenir-sheet details: add small perforation marks, washi tape corners, thin divider rules, route arrows, baggage-tag fragments, a small barcode-style travel archive strip, and tiny handwritten-style notes in Korean.
- Overall arrangement: use the tall poster space as a curated travel archive page, with layered but readable stamps, stickers, captions, and small document-style labels that feel collected over time.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Base layer: build the full-page background first using {배경}, with kraft-paper texture, faint fiber noise, subtle coffee-tinted edges, soft paper bends, and photographed scrapbook depth under studio light.
- Title and archive layer: place the main title "디지털 여권 도장·여행 스티커" near the top, with supporting micro text such as "여권 도장 결", "여행 자랑 인스타 결", "개인 여행 수집 노트", "발행일 2026.05.01", and "스캔 보관용".
- Stamp layer: place {도장 디자인} as the primary repeated motif, varying size, rotation, ink density, and overprint pressure so each country entry feels stamped by hand while remaining legible.
- Country labeling: each stamp for {방문 국가들} should include country name, a compact Korean date treatment such as "2026.05.01", a route code like "ROUTE A-17", and a short caption such as "도착 기록", "하루 산책", or "야시장 메모".
- Sticker layer: add {추가 스티커} as small accent elements around and between the stamps, including travel-ticket shapes, luggage tags, airplane window icons, map-pin stickers, postcard corners, tiny food/travel doodles, and colorful tab labels.
- Collector details: include a small bottom information block with "TRAVEL STICKER ARCHIVE", "NO. 531", "수집일 2026.05", "공유 태그 #여행기록 #스탬프수집", and a barcode-like decorative strip that is clearly graphic, not an official document.
- Color system: apply {컬러 톤} consistently across stamps, sticker outlines, route arrows, caption boxes, and small accents, keeping the palette close to passport ink with colorful sticker highlights.
- Layout finish: use {레이아웃} to control the overall arrangement so the sheet reads as a content-rich curated collection with clear hierarchy, layered paper realism, and visually satisfying travel memorabilia density.
- Format cue: maintain {비율} as a tall poster canvas, with the composition scaled to fill the vertical space elegantly and the collectible page feeling ready to post on Instagram.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold for main country labels and title, Noto Sans KR Medium for smaller date lines, and a compact stamped sans style for serial-like details; all Korean text must stay crisp and highly legible.
- Korean text elements to include naturally: "디지털 여권 도장·여행 스티커", "여권 도장 결", "여행 자랑 인스타 결", "개인 여행 수집 노트", "도착 기록", "수집일 2026.05", "다음 여행은 어디로?".
- Color palette: {컬러 톤} plus kraft brown, beige paper #D8C3A5, off-white #F6F1E8, navy passport ink, faded red entry-stamp ink, teal route accents, and small warm yellow sticker highlights.
- Border/shadow: use subtle ink-edge softness on the stamps, uneven rubber-stamp edges, faint offset print shadow 2px y-offset, 6px blur, 12% opacity, and soft paper-layer shadows beneath stickers and tape.
- Texture realism: add slight ink bleed, imperfect stamp pressure, tiny paper scratches, translucent tape sheen, sticker die-cut outlines, and faint scanner dust specks so the page feels physically collected rather than digitally sterile.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat lay look, simulated with a 50mm lens at f/8 for documentary clarity and even page framing.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left, gentle fill from right, mild paper shadow at lifted sticker edges, controlled highlights on tape and glossy stickers, like a scanned scrapbook page photographed under daylight.
- Color grade: slightly warm paper tone with muted passport-ink contrast, natural paper browns, faded travel-stamp reds and blues, plus restrained color pops for sticker illustrations.
- Realism cue: the final image should look like a real printed collectible souvenir sheet lying flat on textured paper, with believable print registration, tactile edges, and varied ink saturation.

[6. MOOD]
Editorial travel souvenir sheet — feels like a curated Kinfolk x scrapbook collage with the organized energy of a modern passport stamp archive, playful Instagram travel brag energy, and the warmth of a personal journey log.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 다음 한글이 정확히 보여야 함: "디지털 여권 도장·여행 스티커", "여권 도장 결", "여행 자랑 인스타 결"
- Country labels, caption labels, issue-like metadata, and date strings must remain clean and fully readable, with no broken Korean characters.
- The page must clearly read as a decorative collectible travel sticker/stamp sheet, not an official passport page or government document.
- Keep all {방문 국가들}, {도장 디자인}, {추가 스티커}, {배경}, {컬러 톤}, {레이아웃}, and {비율} references intact and visually represented.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[1. PURPOSE]
Travel photo polaroid collage for i2i, designed like a personal diary page with film-print nostalgia, handwritten annotations, travel keepsakes, and small realistic scrapbook details.
Portrait-format memory board that feels like a handmade vacation recap page, suitable for social sharing, printed keepsake use, and a warm travel archive post.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main layout: a vertical 1024x1536 diary page with {6컷 구성} arranged as the primary focus, occupying about 72% of the frame.
- Subject placement: each polaroid sits slightly rotated at varied angles, with several overlapping edges to feel casually assembled by hand after a trip.
- Background treatment: {배경} with visible paper fiber, subtle scuffs, coffee-ring traces, pencil guideline marks, and masking tape securing several corners.
- Scrapbook realism: include {스티커와 소품} around the polaroids, such as a small ticket stub, receipt strip, date label, torn memo paper, pressed leaf, doodled arrows, or washi tape accents.
- Travel context: add a small top label reading "{여행지} 여행 기록" and a date/location stamp using {여행 기간}, integrated like a diary header rather than a formal poster title.
- Keep the original travel-photo identity from {원본 사진}, preserving the people, scenes, and snapshot realism while restyling into a cohesive printed collage.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Full-page base layer — build the entire canvas as a warm scrapbook surface using {배경}, with kraft-paper texture or diary-page grain visible across the page.
2) Header layer — add a casual handwritten or stamped header near the top: "{여행지} 여행 기록", plus a small label such as "{여행 기간}" and "film diary no. 06".
3) Polaroid grid layer — place {6컷 구성} as six separate instant-photo frames, each showing a different travel moment such as food, landscape, selfie, street scene, café detail, market detail, beach walk, train window, or night view.
4) Photo treatment — keep {원본 사진} recognizable inside each frame, with natural travel snapshot crop, mild white borders, tiny print imperfections, and slightly imperfect placement like real printed photos.
5) Tape and overlap details — add several masking tape strips at corners or across one edge, with soft paper shadows to make the collage feel physically assembled.
6) Handwritten annotation layer — place {손글씨 메모} directly beneath each polaroid in black handwritten marker style, slightly uneven baseline and casual spacing; mix short Korean notes, tiny hearts, arrows, and time stamps.
7) Keepsake detail layer — include small travel ephemera such as a torn receipt showing "₩12,000", a mini ticket marked "BOARDING 09:40", a location tag "{여행지}", a page number "PAGE 01/06", and a tiny social caption strip with "{작성자 핸들}".
8) Color unification layer — apply {컬러 톤} across the full composition so all six images feel like one coherent printed memory set.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: handwritten note style resembling neat marker pen or casual brush pen, 18–28 px visual size, slightly irregular stroke width; small date stamps and receipt text may use compact monoline printed lettering.
- Korean text: all handwritten notes and labels must be legible Korean, with natural spacing and casual diary phrasing.
- Color palette: kraft brown, warm cream, black ink, muted teal, faded coral, dusty amber, soft sage, and soft sepia from {컬러 톤}; use paper tones like #D8C3A5, #F5EBDD, #2B2B2B, #A67C52.
- Border/shadow: polaroid borders should be matte white with a soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; tape should cast a faint translucent shadow and show fibrous texture.
- Decorative details: keep stickers, stamps, tickets, doodles, and tape physically plausible, as if placed on an actual travel diary page.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm or 50mm travel snapshot look, as if shot on a compact film camera or smartphone then printed as instant photos; mild depth, no extreme wide-angle distortion.
- Lighting: natural daylight travel lighting, softly diffused like overcast afternoon or shaded street light, with gentle highlights and no harsh flash burn.
- Color grade: warm film scan grade with slightly lifted blacks, soft grain, faded highlights, and nostalgic brown/amber bias matching {컬러 톤}.
- Material rendering: matte instant-photo paper, kraft fiber, washi tape translucency, ink bleed on paper, tiny dust specks, and soft contact shadows between layers.

[6. MOOD]
Personal travel diary page — Kinfolk scrapbook spread meets analog film print aesthetic, like a cherished handmade vacation memory board with ticket stubs, taped memories, and warm handwritten afterthoughts.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구들이 손글씨 메모로 정확히 보여야 함: "제주 흑돼지 진심", "한라산 일출 ♥".
- Additional visible Korean details should include: "{여행지} 여행 기록", "또 가고 싶은 날", "오늘의 발견", "날씨 맑음", and "{대표 캡션}".
- Preserve the identity of the original travel photos inside {원본 사진}; faces, scenes, and scene relationships should remain recognizable after collage treatment.
- Keep all six frames as distinct polaroid prints with visible white borders; do not merge them into one flat poster.
- Maintain a handmade diary collage look with slight rotation, overlap, paper shadows, tape, stickers, and travel ephemera, not a perfectly aligned corporate layout.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Misleading passport, visa, or government-document replicas
- Celebrity composites without explicit reference consent

studio:prompts3:ours-529.content:
[INPUT]
- reference_image: {원본 인물}
- language: Korean

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean school milestone commemorative photo transformation, i2i portrait-style square image for entrance ceremony, graduation, or exam-finish celebration.
Keep the subject identity from {원본 인물} while converting it into a polished, real-looking school-studio commemorative portrait with authentic ceremony details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the subject as a single hero portrait occupying about 65% of the frame, with formal school-photo framing and enough surrounding context to show the event atmosphere.
- Preserve the facial identity and pose relationship of {원본 인물}, while adapting the scene to {기념 종류} with a neat, celebratory, memory-album composition.
- Keep the background as a recognizable school setting described by {배경}, enriched with realistic Korean school details such as a gate banner, classroom board, bouquet table, hallway bulletin board, playground fence, or graduation photo zone.
- Dress the subject in {의상 결}, with realistic fabric structure, collar edges, badge or emblem placement, pressed seams, and photo-ready fitting.
- Use {자세} as the main pose structure, ensuring natural shoulder alignment, upright posture, and believable interaction with props if present.
- Add subtle commemorative card elements around the photo area: a small date/location label, a short Korean caption, and tasteful sticker-like tags that match {기념 종류} without overpowering the portrait.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground subject: {원본 인물} rendered as a school commemorative portrait with crisp facial detail, realistic skin texture, natural hair detail, and clear photographic separation from the background.
- Outfit layer: apply {의상 결} with accurate folds, seams, buttons, ribbon/tie shape, blazer lapels, uniform emblem, gown fabric, or ceremony accessories depending on {기념 종류}.
- Pose and hands: follow {자세}; if hands are visible, keep them anatomically correct, naturally relaxed, and proportional to the body. If appropriate, the subject may hold a small bouquet, diploma tube, admission placard, class photo booklet, or exam-finish congratulatory card.
- Background layer: build {배경} as a school-event backdrop with a front gate, classroom wall, hallway, playground, auditorium curtain, or photo-zone feel. Include event signage appropriate to {기념 종류}, such as “입학을 축하합니다”, “졸업을 축하합니다”, or “수고했어, 새로운 시작!” in readable Korean.
- Commemorative overlay layer: include realistic small printed details like “2026.03.02”, “서울 ○○초등학교”, “3학년 2반”, “Memory Photo”, “#새출발”, or “오늘의 주인공” where suitable; keep them integrated as a printed card/photo-frame design rather than a flashy ad.
- Lighting layer: maintain the school photo studio look with even frontal illumination, gentle shadow control, catchlights in the eyes, and soft highlight separation so the face stays clear and presentable.
- Color layer: apply {컬러 톤} across skin, clothing, background, signage, and card accents so the final image feels like a scanned Korean school commemorative photo with modern retouching.
- Format layer: keep everything perfectly square in {비율}, with the subject centered and the composition stable for profile, family sharing, or memory-book use.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: event text and labels should use clean Korean sans-serif such as Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, medium to bold weight, with sharp edges and realistic print/photo-zone placement.
- Korean text examples to render only when contextually appropriate: “입학을 축하합니다”, “졸업 축하해”, “새로운 시작”, “2026년 봄”, “우리 반 추억”, “수고했어 오늘도”.
- Color palette: prioritize white, warm amber, soft beige, muted navy, gentle sky blue, pastel pink, and school-photo neutrals; keep tones close to {컬러 톤} and avoid saturated neon colors.
- Decorative details: use tasteful ceremony elements such as ribbon stickers, paper confetti, a small flower illustration, school crest-like graphic decoration without official seal styling, notebook lines, film-strip corners, or a printed photo-card label.
- Border/shadow: use subtle photographic separation only, such as a soft drop shadow with 3px vertical offset, 10px blur, and 12% opacity if needed.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: DSLR school portrait look, 50mm f/2.8 standard portrait framing, straight-on perspective, minimal distortion.
- Lighting: even front-facing studio-style light with soft fill from both sides, gentle top ambient balance, and controlled highlights; emulate a Korean school photo studio setup while retaining realistic environmental depth.
- Color grade: natural light + white + warm amber with mild contrast, clean skin tones, lightly softened background, and a slightly nostalgic school-photo finish.
- Detail rendering: realistic fabric weave, school signage print texture, bouquet petals or ribbon edges if present, subtle paper grain on caption labels, and natural lens depth between subject and background.

[6. MOOD]
Classic Korean school commemorative portrait — polished yearbook / graduation album aesthetic with a warm, proud, family-keepsake tone. The image should feel like a real milestone photo taken on an important school day, not a sterile studio mockup.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: any visible event signage, date label, caption, sticker, or school-style label must be clean Korean with no broken characters or misspellings.
- Preserve identity: {원본 인물} must remain recognizably the same person, with no face reshaping that changes identity.
- Pose and anatomy: keep body proportions realistic, hands anatomically correct, and the overall framing stable in square format.
- If a banner, sign, caption, or sticker label is included, its Korean wording must be event-appropriate to {기념 종류} and visually readable.
- Keep {의상 결}, {배경}, {자세}, {컬러 톤}, and {비율} clearly reflected in the final image.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Sexualized styling or revealing clothing emphasis
- Distorted facial identity or unrelated celebrity replacement

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]

[4. STYLE RULES]

- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at 45°, with a gentle fill from the right and no harsh specular highlights.
- Color grade: warm cream + amber + coral + muted sage, with slightly lowered contrast and smooth tonal transitions.
- Material detail: tactile matte paper, watercolor pigment edges, gentle ink bleed on Korean lettering, satin ribbon highlights, and softly layered floral illustration.

[6. MOOD]

Korean newlywed home interior mood board, style-by-style 4-panel collage for inspiration, budgeting, and planning.
Editorial A4 mood board layout designed for Pinterest, Instagram carousel cover, wedding-prep community sharing, and interior consultation reference.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Vertical A4-style canvas, full-page collage with 4 interior reference blocks arranged in a polished grid, each block occupying roughly 22–24% of the frame with consistent gutters and magazine-like alignment.
- The overall composition should feel like a curated Korean interior magazine planning page: tactile, layered, realistic, and useful for a couple comparing design directions.
- Background treatment: warm off-white paper surface with subtle matte grain, visible paper fibers, taped corners, small pencil guide marks, fabric tabs, and material sample overlaps.
- Use {컨셉 스타일} as the main styling direction, and map {공간 별 레퍼런스} into the collage blocks with visible sofas, bedding, dining objects, tiles, faucets, curtains, rugs, lighting, books, ceramics, plants, and color accents.
- Place {텍스트 레이블} as compact labels near each block, ensuring the hierarchy reads like a premium interior lookbook with practical planning notes.
- Add realistic editorial metadata: {발행 정보}, {프로젝트명}, {촬영/제작 날짜}, {위치 라벨}, and a small vertical spine credit on the left edge reading {스파인 크레딧}.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header band (about 12–15% height): set the title area as an editorial masthead with strong Korean typography, include the main title, VOL/date line, and a small subtitle for newlywed home planning.
2. Main collage field (about 70–75% height): build four reference panels with clearly distinct visual identities, each panel showing interior surfaces, furniture silhouettes, decor props, lighting fixtures, and lived-in styling details rather than empty rooms.
3. Label overlay system: attach {텍스트 레이블} to each panel as small tag-like captions, with room name, concept keyword, estimated mood, and one short note such as “러그 추천”, “조명 포인트”, “수납 아이디어”, or “타일 샘플”.
4. Palette integration: weave {컬러 팔레트} into textiles, wall tones, wood finishes, ceramics, cushions, books, framed art, towels, tiles, grout, metal fixtures, and accent objects so each style reads immediately.
5. Texture layer: combine {비주얼 결} with paper cutout edges, real-looking sample swatches, linen scraps, wood veneer chips, stone/tile chips, paint cards, masking tape, binder clips, and small handwritten arrows.
6. Footer information area (about 8–10% height): include {예산 메모}, {체크리스트}, a tiny QR-style consultation box labeled {QR 라벨}, and contact-style studio text {문의 정보} as part of the magazine mood-board design.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for labels, SemiBold to Bold for headers, 22–34px for title hierarchy, 14–18px for captions, 9–12px for metadata and micro notes, with crisp Korean rendering.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} as the primary set, anchored by off-white #F4F0E8, soft gray #D8D5CF, warm wood brown #A67C52, muted sage #A9B8A6, charcoal #2F2F2F, plus small metallic or ceramic accents if they fit the selected style.
- Border/shadow: thin paper-cut separators, soft drop shadows with 3px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity, layered overlap depth under clipped image blocks, tape strips, stickers, and material swatch shadows.
- Magazine details: include small page number, issue marker, category tag, caption rule lines, and a discreet barcode-like graphic that reads as editorial decoration, not a real product code.
- Visual richness: allow realistic household styling details such as mugs, slippers, cushions, open books, towels, soap bottles, spice jars, plants, art prints, vases, fabric wrinkles, tile grout, wood grain, and small planning annotations.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Canon EOS R5 editorial interior photography feel; 24mm wide-angle for room context and 50mm standard lens for detail crops, f/4 to f/5.6 for clean clarity.
- Lighting: soft diffused daylight from upper-left, gentle ambient fill, believable shadows under paper layers, natural highlights on ceramic, glass, wood, linen, metal, and stone surfaces.
- Color grade: neutral warm whites, muted earth tones, low-saturation greens, charcoal accents, soft beige paper, natural wood warmth, and a calm showroom-like tonal balance.
- Print realism: emulate a premium interior magazine collage with slightly uneven cut edges, high-resolution photo texture, visible matte ink, tactile swatches, and subtle scanner-like paper depth.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean interior design editorial — warm, useful, newlywed-focused, tactile, aspirational, and realistic, like a studio-made lookbook page prepared before purchasing furniture and finishing materials.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear exactly and clearly: "신혼집 인테리어 무드보드", "컨셉 스타일", "공간 별 레퍼런스", "컬러 팔레트", "텍스트 레이블", "비주얼 결".
- Also render these planning details clearly in Korean: "{발행 정보}", "{프로젝트명}", "{촬영/제작 날짜}", "{위치 라벨}", "{예산 메모}", "{체크리스트}", "{문의 정보}".
- Maintain a strict 4-panel collage structure with consistent spacing, aligned gutters, and no additional room panels beyond the four planned interior reference blocks.
- Every Korean label, caption, price note, date, and micro annotation must be fully legible, correctly spaced, and free of broken characters or garbling.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity face composites or portrait-style people photography
- Fake government, bank, or legal-document styling

Modern Korean wedding invitation card for a mobile-friendly vertical format, clean editorial layout with elegant typography and realistic wedding-card information.
Designed for a Korean couple’s wedding announcement, with premium ivory stationery texture, subtle botanical detail, monogram accent, family/RSVP details, and polished digital invitation readability.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main title area sits in the upper 16% of the canvas, centered, with refined letter spacing and a small issue-card-like date badge.
- Event information block occupies the middle 36% with clear hierarchy: {신랑} ♥ {신부}, {예식일시}, {장소}, and {주소} on carefully separated lines.
- Signature motif is placed between title and information block as {시그니처 모티프}, combining a small botanical drawing, initials monogram, and a fine gold accent.
- Greeting text {인사말} sits below the core details, centered, with a short two-line cadence suitable for a Korean wedding invitation.
- Lower information area includes {혼주}, {연락처}, {RSVP마감}, {드레스코드}, a small map/QR-style guide label {약도라벨}, and a discreet calendar mark {달력표기}.
- Background is warm ivory paper texture with tactile grain, faint letterpress impression, soft deckled-paper realism, and delicate foil-like micro rules.
- Use {컨셉} and {컬러 팔레트} to guide the full stationery treatment: typography, botanical motif, micro icons, divider lines, date badge, and accent marks.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header area: set the invitation title as “WEDDING INVITATION” with wide tracking, deep charcoal ink, centered near the top, plus a tiny Korean label “모시는 글” beneath it.
2. Date badge: place {달력표기} as a small refined calendar capsule or circular stamp-like graphic near the title area, using sage or muted gold linework.
3. Name/date block: render “{신랑}  ♥  {신부}” as the primary text line in the largest font weight, with the names emphasized and a delicate heart or centered dot separator.
4. Event details: place {예식일시}, {장소}, and {주소} beneath the names, each on its own line, with clear hierarchy and elegant spacing.
5. Motif zone: render {시그니처 모티프} as a botanical ornament, olive branch, small flower line illustration, or initials monogram, printed like subtle foil or ink.
6. Greeting block: place {인사말} centered in the lower-middle area, using a softer serif or light sans style and comfortable line height.
7. Family and RSVP block: add {혼주}, {연락처}, {RSVP마감}, and {드레스코드} in a compact lower section separated by fine rules and small icons such as phone, calendar, location pin, and envelope.
8. Map/guide detail: include a tiny map-card hint, QR-style square placeholder, or venue guide label reading {약도라벨}, integrated as a realistic mobile invitation utility element.
9. Concept treatment: express {컨셉} through modern editorial balance, warm paper, refined ink weight, and tasteful botanical/foil accents rather than excessive ornament.
10. Palette application: apply {컬러 팔레트} to text accents, motif, hairline dividers, date capsule, and micro icons while keeping high contrast for Korean readability.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for main Korean text, weight 500–700, with a clean modern sans for hierarchy; optional subtle serif accent such as Noto Serif KR for the greeting line.
- Color palette: use {컬러 팔레트} with concrete application such as ivory #F7F3EA, sage green #A8B8A3, muted gold #C8A96A, and charcoal #2A2A2A.
- Paper and print finish: warm ivory cotton-paper grain, slight letterpress depth on key text, muted gold foil glint on the motif and thin separators, realistic ink edges.
- Graphic details: fine dividers, small calendar capsule, location pin, envelope icon, QR-style guide square, botanical corner sprigs, and monogram initials may appear as part of the invitation design.
- Hierarchy: couple names and date must read first, venue second, greeting and family/RSVP details third, with all Korean text sharp and legible.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down stationery mockup feel, equivalent to a 50mm standard lens on a flat editorial setup, crisp and distortion-free.
- Lighting: soft diffuse studio light from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from right, even illumination with natural paper shadows and mild foil highlights.
- Color grade: warm ivory base with muted sage and soft gold accents, low saturation, calm premium print-editorial tonality.

[6. MOOD]
Premium Korean wedding stationery — modern editorial, warm ivory paper, refined botanical romance, quiet luxury, and trustworthy mobile invitation polish.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: "박지호", "이서윤", "2026.06.07 (토) 12:30", "신라호텔 영빈관", "서울 중구 동호로 249", "두 사람의 작은 시작에 함께해주세요".
- 추가로 자연스럽게 표시할 문구: "모시는 글", "WEDDING INVITATION", "혼주 박성민·김혜진 / 이정훈·최미라", "RSVP 2026.05.25까지", "문의 010-2470-0607", "단정한 세미포멀", "약도 및 주차 안내".

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean study-method card news for high-stakes exam prep, vertical editorial infographic for social sharing.
A premium educational card-news page for {대상 시험} learners, presenting five memorization and practice strategies in a realistic social-media study guide format with editorial metadata, slide navigation, and practical exam-planning details.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Canvas: A4 portrait vertical composition, tall 1024x1536 framing with strong top-to-bottom reading flow and a polished Instagram carousel / academy handout feel.
- Main title zone occupies the upper 16% of the frame, with an editorial label such as "STUDY NEWS", issue tag "VOL.247", date label "2026.05 SPECIAL", and slide indicator "01/06" placed around the masthead.
- Use {대상 시험} as the top context line, and structure the middle content around {5가지 공부법} as the main information stack.
- Visual language should combine {시각화} with crisp box modules, clear dividers, small academic icons, tabs, page markers, and planner-like annotations that feel like a real study strategy card saved from a learning account.
- Background treatment: deep matte navy surface with subtle paper grain, faint off-white grid texture, study-note tick marks, small gold corner rules, and layered editorial panels that create a finished magazine-card-news page.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area (top 16%): place a strong Korean masthead reading "공부법 카드뉴스", with {대상 시험} directly beneath in smaller supporting type; add small credit text such as "Editor. 합격전략팀", "Study Lab Archive", "VOL.247", and "2026년 5월호".
- Intro strip (below header): include a short Korean explanatory line such as "오늘부터 바로 적용하는 5단계 회독 루틴" and a small label chip reading "저장용 요약본" before transitioning into the main five-item framework using {5가지 공부법} as the content source.
- Main information area (mid 60%): build five stacked or modular boxes, each box clearly separated and numbered 01–05, with one study method per box; integrate {시각화} as small illustrative symbols beside each item, such as a clock, flashcard, pencil, graph, checkbox, mini calendar, or memory map.
- Each method card should contain a short Korean headline, one compact supporting sentence, and a tiny action tag such as "복습", "기출", "암기", "오답", "회독" so the page feels like a usable study plan rather than a blank template.
- Progress / utility area (lower section): show a slim 진도 바, checklist markers, a weekly repetition cue, and a page indicator line such as "1 / 6  다음 장: 실전 적용표"; include tiny save/share/bookmark micro icons in the lower corner like a real card-news post.
- Footer area (bottom 10%): add a concise guide-note closing line such as "저장하고 오늘 공부 루틴에 바로 적용해보세요" plus a small CTA "다음 카드에서 예시 플래너 확인" and a handle-style credit "@study.archive".

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold for the title, Pretendard SemiBold or Noto Sans KR Medium for section headers, and Pretendard Regular for explanatory body text; title size should be large and compact, with body text sized for infographic readability.
- Color palette: deep navy #0E1B2E, white #F7F7F4, muted gold #C8A85A, cool gray #A9B4C2, and a subtle paper-beige highlight for contrast; reflect {컬러 톤} through accent chips, divider lines, and small infographic marks.
- Border/shadow: use thin gold divider lines, 1px or 2px strokes, soft drop shadows at 4px y-offset, 12px blur, about 15% opacity for each content card, plus small printed-paper texture and layered label stickers.
- Keep all modules editorial and consistent, with squared corners or slightly rounded corners, steady padding, visible numbering, utility icons, page navigation marks, and decorative academic details that support the study theme.
- Maintain {비율} as the overall proportion logic for the title, content blocks, progress area, and footer so the composition reads as a finished vertical carousel cover page.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat editorial infographic look, referenced to Canon EOS R5 product-photo clarity with a 50mm lens perspective, rendered as a precise graphic layout rather than a photographed scene.
- Lighting: simulated soft studio top-light with even diffusion, gentle card shadows, and a slight vignette to anchor the navy background.
- Color grade: deep navy + white + gold academic palette, with precise highlight control and crisp readable contrast; use the grid, paper grain, and gold accents to make the design feel tactile and publication-ready.

[6. MOOD]
Premium study-guide magazine spread — calm, disciplined, information-dense, and practical like a university exam-prep handbook transformed into a polished Korean card-news carousel.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: "공부법 카드뉴스", "{대상 시험}", "{5가지 공부법}", "{시각화}", "{컬러 톤}", "{비율}"
- Include realistic card-news details in Korean: "VOL.247", "2026년 5월호", "01/06", "저장용 요약본", "다음 장: 실전 적용표", "@study.archive".
- All five study methods must be clearly distinguishable as separate items, with numbering 01–05 preserved and no merged or duplicated boxes.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean fitness routine infographic card, 5-step vertical guide for home workout, gym, and stretching use.
Create a realistic premium social-media card that feels like a saved workout plan from a fitness coach: clear steps, timing/reps, small tracking details, and a concise result line.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Portrait A4-style vertical layout with a strong top-to-bottom reading flow; title band at top 14%, five stacked step panels in the middle 72%, and a slim result/CTA strip at bottom 14%.
- Each step panel should be equally spaced with a precise editorial grid, bold numbering on the left, exercise name and count/time information in the center, and a simple exercise visual from {시각화} on the right.
- Background: matte dark charcoal field with tactile sports-card paper texture, faint gym-floor linework, subtle grain, tiny measurement ticks, and layered lime green accent bars that match {컬러 톤}.
- Add realistic card-news details: small slide label “ROUTINE 01”, date label “2026.05”, handle “@daily.fit.note”, tiny save/share icons, a page indicator “1/5 GUIDE”, and a compact CTA such as “저장하고 오늘 따라하기”.
- Use {루틴 종류}, {5단계 운동}, {시각화}, {효과 한 줄}, {컬러 톤}, {비율} as editable placeholders in the layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header band (top 14%): place the main title as a large Korean headline, for example “5단계 운동 루틴”, centered or slightly left-aligned, with a compact subtitle line beneath it using {루틴 종류}; include small editorial metadata such as “VOL.520”, “2026년 5월 루틴”, “10–20 MIN”, and “BEGINNER OK”.
- Header micro-elements: add a thin lime progress bar, tiny checklist marks, and a small label “오늘의 코칭 카드” to make the design feel like a real published card-news asset.
- Step 1 panel: show the first item from {5단계 운동} as a numbered block “01” with a simple exercise illustration from {시각화}; include a lime badge such as “40초” or “12회”, a tiny rest label “휴식 15초”, and a small Korean cue line like “호흡 먼저 정리”.
- Step 2 panel: repeat the same structure for the second item from {5단계 운동}, maintaining identical card width, spacing, and badge placement; add a small motion arrow, rep counter chip, and micro note like “무릎·허리 체크”.
- Step 3 panel: place the third item from {5단계 운동} with the same visual language; use {시각화} as a clean fitness illustration with subtle body-position guide lines, a mat/dumbbell/resistance-band motif if appropriate, and a short cue such as “천천히 컨트롤”.
- Step 4 panel: present the fourth item from {5단계 운동} with clear rep/time formatting, slightly larger number emphasis than the label, a crisp white panel edge, and a tiny intensity marker “강도 ★★★☆☆”.
- Step 5 panel: present the fifth item from {5단계 운동} as the final step, with a stronger lime accent line to signal completion; include a finishing cue such as “마무리 스트레칭” or “심박 안정” while preserving the same panel geometry.
- Bottom result strip (last 14%): set {효과 한 줄} in a bold condensed Korean line, centered and highly legible; add small supporting text “완료 체크 □  오늘 기록하기”, “다음 루틴: 강도 조절”, and a tiny page/footer indicator “FIT ROUTINE CARD / SAVE & SHARE”.
- Apply {컬러 톤} consistently across titles, badges, divider lines, icons, progress bars, and accent bars; preserve the same A4 vertical ratio from {비율}.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold for the main title, Pretendard SemiBold for step labels, and Noto Sans KR Medium for counts/time badges; title around 54–64 px, step labels 24–30 px, badges 18–22 px, metadata 12–16 px.
- Color palette: dark charcoal #1E1F23, lime green #B8FF3D, white #F7F7F4, cool gray #AAB0B8, with tiny black outline text if needed for contrast; keep {컬러 톤} visible in every major accent.
- Border/shadow: thin white panel borders at 2 px, subtle drop shadow 0px 6px 18px at 14% opacity, realistic printed-card grain, fine divider rules, and small UI-style icon strokes.
- Graphic details should feel practical and coach-made: rep chips, timer icons, rest markers, checkboxes, thin arrows, section labels, and small Korean cue text arranged neatly inside the grid.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: studio graphic poster look inspired by a clean editorial fitness infographic, as if composed front-on with a 50mm standard lens perspective and flat graphic layout, not a live workout photo.
- Lighting: even diffused studio illumination with slight top-left emphasis to separate panels from the charcoal background; paper texture and subtle shadows should give the card a real printed/digital publication feel.
- Color grade: high-contrast charcoal, lime, and white with controlled saturation, resembling a modern gym-class poster, performance-tracking app card, and Korean Instagram card-news design.
- Exercise visuals: simple illustrated figures or icon-like diagrams from {시각화}, with motion lines, position guides, small equipment silhouettes, and clear posture cues.

[6. MOOD]
Modern fitness coaching infographic — crisp performance-tracker aesthetic with the discipline of a premium training app card and the clarity of an editorial Korean exercise guide. Energetic, useful, saved-for-later, and realistic enough to look like an actual fitness account post.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구는 {루틴 종류}, {5단계 운동}, {효과 한 줄}의 렌더링 텍스트이며, 각 단계의 번호와 운동명은 오탈자 없이 선명하게 읽혀야 한다.
- Include readable Korean microcopy such as “저장하고 오늘 따라하기”, “휴식 15초”, “완료 체크”, “오늘의 코칭 카드”, and “2026년 5월 루틴” without broken characters.
- Layout invariant: exactly 5 stacked steps, all panels aligned to the same grid, with consistent spacing and no missing step.
- The visual treatment must remain card-news style, structured, and easy to follow, using simple exercise illustrations rather than live-action photography.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

- Broken Korean characters
- Extra steps beyond the exact 5-step structure

Korean weekly meal-plan card for dieting, solo living, and healthy meal prep. Designed as an A4 vertical editorial infographic that feels like a real printed planner page photographed for social sharing, with practical meal details, nutrition cues, and lifestyle-magazine warmth.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Center the full 7-day meal schedule as the main subject, occupying about 78% of the frame, with a slim top title band, a detailed main schedule grid, and a bottom summary band.

- Present the meal plan as a slightly tactile printed card on warm cream paper, photographed top-down on a natural kitchen-table surface with subtle paper fiber, faint ink texture, and tiny realistic print imperfections.
- Add realistic planner context around the card edges without interfering with readability: a small pencil, measuring spoon, folded sticky note, two cherry tomatoes or herb leaves, and a tiny washi-tape corner detail in tones matching {컬러 톤}.
- The card should include a clear editorial hierarchy: title, week/date metadata, 7-day meal grid, nutrition summary, shopping memo, and prep-note strip.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header band (about 12%): set the title as a strong Korean masthead, with a short subtitle area for {식단 컨셉}; include practical metadata such as WEEK 21, 2026.05.18–05.24, 냉장고 파먹기 플랜, and 1인분 기준 in small supporting type.
- Add a compact label row under the masthead with short Korean tags: 다이어트 1500kcal, 자취 5천원, 헬스 고단백, 비건, 한식 가정식; style them as rounded chips or stamped labels.
- Main grid body (about 68%): build the 7-column × 3-row schedule using {레이아웃}, where each day column contains three meal cells for 아침, 점심, 저녁; every cell contains a small food illustration, calorie number, and a concise ingredient note from {요일별 메뉴}.
- Day labels: place the weekday labels 월, 화, 수, 목, 금, 토, 일 at the top of each column with clear hierarchy; include tiny date numerals beneath each weekday for a real planner feel.
- Meal cells: align each meal block within the grid so the illustration sits above the calorie text and the ingredient note sits below, all evenly padded; use small hand-drawn food icons such as 현미밥, 닭가슴살, 두부샐러드, 계란, 그릭요거트, 된장국, 고구마, 오트밀, 채소볶음, and 과일.
- Decorative system: integrate {장식 요소} as lively but controlled health-editorial details: tiny leaf marks, check circles, water-drop icons, vegetable doodles, dotted dividers, sticker-like labels, and small tape marks at grid corners.
- Right or lower micro-info strip: add a compact weekly checklist with Korean items such as 물 2L, 단백질 챙기기, 야식 줄이기, 장보기 완료, each with small checkboxes.
- Bottom summary band (about 10%): reserve a boxed area for total calories and a small weekly summary; include 총 섭취 목표 10,500kcal, 평균 1,500kcal, 단백질 95g 목표, 장보기 예산 ₩35,000, and a mini shopping list line: 달걀 · 닭가슴살 · 두부 · 현미 · 제철채소.
- Include small footer details like @meal.note, VOL.07, printable planner, and page marker 01/01 to make the card feel complete and publishable.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard ExtraBold for the main title, Pretendard SemiBold for weekday labels and meal names, and Pretendard Regular for calorie notes, ingredient notes, footer metadata, and checklist text; title size large, labels medium, notes small but crisp and readable.
- Color palette: cream beige, muted green, and charcoal based on {컬러 톤}; use off-white #F4F0E6, sage green #8FAE8C, deep charcoal #2F343A, oat beige #D8CBB2, tomato red accent #C95F4B, and soft warm gray for secondary text.
- Border/shadow: use thin 1px dividers in charcoal at low opacity, subtle rounded card edges, lightly imperfect printed lines, and a soft drop shadow of 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity for the summary box and sticker labels.
- Illustration style: small editorial food drawings should look printed on paper with natural pigment variation, not sterile vector icons; keep ingredients recognizable and appetizing.
- Text density: make the schedule content-rich like a real meal-prep planner, with short Korean labels, calorie figures, portion notes, and ingredient snippets while keeping the 7-column × 3-row structure readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat-lay editorial look, equivalent to a 35mm lens perspective at f/5.6 for crisp document-like clarity.
- Lighting: soft diffused daylight from upper-left at about 45°, with gentle natural shadows from the card, pencil, spoon, sticky note, and herbs; slight bounce fill from the right to keep all Korean text readable.
- Color grade: warm cream paper base with sage accents and restrained charcoal contrast, similar to a modern health magazine infographic photographed on a calm kitchen table.
- Material realism: visible paper tooth, faint ink absorption at text edges, subtle pressed-card thickness, tiny tape texture, and realistic contact shadows so the image feels photographed rather than a flat digital mockup.

[6. MOOD]
Editorial health-planner aesthetic — like a Kinfolk-style meal prep spread combined with a clean Japanese lifestyle magazine layout, practical enough for dieting, solo living, and weekly grocery planning.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear clearly and without broken characters: "일주일 식단표 카드", "다이어트 1500kcal", "자취 5천원", "헬스 고단백", "비건", "한식 가정식", "월", "화", "수", "목", "금", "토", "일".
- Additional Korean text should be realistic and legible, including short planner details such as "아침", "점심", "저녁", "총 섭취 목표", "평균 1,500kcal", "장보기 예산 ₩35,000", "물 2L", "단백질 챙기기", and "장보기 완료".
- The 7-column × 3-row grid must remain consistent across all days.
- Each cell must contain a food illustration, calorie text, and a small ingredient note in the same relative order.
- The bottom total-calorie summary box must stay visible and separated from the main grid.
- The surrounding kitchen-table props must remain secondary and must not cover any Korean text or break the schedule structure.

[1. PURPOSE]
Realistic phone front-camera selfie photo at a night sports venue, portrait vertical format for social sharing.
Close-up, casual unposed feel with authentic low-light smartphone capture, enriched with believable stadium details and a subtle social-post layer.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- {원본 인물} should fill about 70% of the frame, with the face centered slightly above midline and the arm-length perspective kept obvious.
- Background uses {환경} as a visible but slightly blurred context layer, with stadium structure, artificial turf or court markings, net/fence lines, floodlight poles, benches, and a few distant people receding naturally behind the subject.
- Keep the framing tight around the head and shoulders, like a real phone selfie taken just after or during a night game, with imperfect cropping and a little venue depth visible around the edges.
- Outfit visibility should remain clear enough for {의상} to read as a sports selfie; show shoulders and upper chest, fabric texture, seams, sweat or slight wrinkles where natural, while the face remains the main focal point.
- Add subtle social selfie details: a small date/location sticker near one upper corner and a tiny casual caption sticker near the lower edge, integrated like an Instagram Story overlay without covering the face.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Foreground hero (main 70%): {원본 인물} rendered as a realistic close-up selfie, with natural facial proportions, front-camera perspective, and slight arm extension distortion kept subtle.
- Midground context (15–20%): {의상} visible from shoulders to upper chest, matching the casual sports setting; include realistic collar folds, jersey/hoodie texture, small reflective highlights, and natural low-light color shifts.
- Background environment (15–20%): {환경} with stadium lighting, fence lines, goalpost or court/field markings, a sideline bench, water bottles or sports bags in the distance, and distant players/spectators softly blurred to preserve the selfie feel.
- Social overlay elements: add one small rounded location/date tag reading '5월 18일 · 야간 경기장', one tiny caption tag reading '오늘도 한 경기 완료', and a small decorative sticker such as a star, whistle, ball icon, or lightning shape; make them look like app overlay graphics, not printed signage.
- Face rendering: {자세·표정} with direct eye contact, relaxed cheeks, and an authentic candid expression rather than a studio portrait.
- Light behavior: {조명·결} should create uneven face illumination, bright highlights from overhead venue lights, occasional lens flare or glow near floodlights, soft under-eye shadowing, and gentle noise/grain consistent with a real phone photo.
- Final image handling: {후처리·결} must preserve natural skin texture, slight sensor noise, tiny motion softness, and imperfect phone framing; keep the result believable as a casual night selfie.
- Canvas format: {비율} with a strong vertical phone-photo layout suitable for a natural selfie post.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography / overlay: use only small Korean social-story overlay text, accurate and readable: '5월 18일 · 야간 경기장' and '오늘도 한 경기 완료'. Keep it subtle, clean, and secondary to the face.
- Color palette: slightly cool night tones, stadium-white highlights, muted greens from the field, dark navy shadows, neutral skin tones, and small pops of app-sticker color such as yellow, blue, or white.
- Border/shadow: no artificial frame is needed; use natural shadows from the selfie lighting, venue lights, and soft glow around background floodlights.
- Environmental realism: include believable night-sports details such as turf texture, painted field lines, chain-link fence, metal bleachers, scoreboard glow, team bags, and distant blurred movement.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: smartphone front camera, equivalent to a 24–26mm full-frame field of view, arm’s-length selfie perspective, slight edge distortion.
- Lighting: bright stadium floodlights from above and slightly behind the camera, creating uneven facial highlights, soft under-eye shadowing, catchlights in the eyes, a faint halo around hair edges, and a luminous blurred background.
- Color grade: real-night phone photo grade with slightly cool white balance, muted saturation, mild low-light noise, small compression artifacts, and natural dynamic-range limitations; no polished studio finish.

[6. MOOD]
Authentic casual night-sports selfie — like a candid Instagram Story captured on a phone at a lit football field after a game, energetic but natural, personal, and lived-in.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: render the overlay text clearly as '5월 18일 · 야간 경기장' and '오늘도 한 경기 완료'; any background Korean signage must be legible or softly blurred, never broken.
- Do not change the subject's facial features.
- Maintain realistic selfie framing, front-camera perspective, and natural low-light imperfections exactly.
- Keep the expression casual, neutral, and slightly playful rather than staged.
- Ensure social stickers and captions remain small and do not cover the eyes, nose, mouth, or defining facial features.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals/certifications
- 한글 깨짐
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

[6. MOOD]
Nostalgic, intimate night-walk memory — like a quiet A24 urban still or a candid Japanese street diary photo, but with Korean alley details, soft city noise, and the feeling of a private moment accidentally preserved.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header zone (top 12%): title area with editorial hierarchy; include large Korean title “퍼스널 컬러 분석”, smaller subtitle “나에게 어울리는 온도와 채도”, report number “REPORT NO. PC-0526”, date label “2026.05”, and a small credit line “Colorist: Studio Ours”.

4. Best Palette zone (right column mid 28%): {Best Palette 컬러칩} arranged as multiple rounded rectangular swatches in a 2-column or 3-column grid, each chip with small Korean color names such as “크림 베이지”, “세이지”, “카멜”, “테라코타”, “더스티 올리브”, “소프트 브라운”.

7. Footer zone (bottom 8%): thin divider rule, compact caption area, page marker “01 / PERSONAL COLOR”, small disclaimer-style text “개인 피부 톤과 조명에 따라 차이가 있을 수 있습니다”, and a tiny barcode/QR-style graphic block for a realistic printed report finish.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR, bold for headers 700, regular for labels 400, small tracking for section titles, with {레이아웃·타이포} guiding the editorial hierarchy and legibility.

[7. CRITICAL]

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

1) Hero portrait zone: place {콩트 캐릭터} in a front-facing close-up, with exaggerated {분장 결} clearly readable from the first glance; keep the face large, centered, and dominant.
2) Expression and gesture zone: render {자세·표정} with obvious comic timing, using facial tension, hand gesture, and costume details to reinforce the sketch character identity.
3) Caption box zone: add a large rectangular Korean text box across the lower portion, with {메인 자막} set in bold, high-contrast typography and {에피소드 라벨} as a small tag nearby.
4) Hook and sticker zone: place {조회 유도 문구}, {강조 이모지}, arrows, burst stickers, and a small reaction-style graphic around the portrait to create clickable YouTube thumbnail energy.

7) Thumbnail clarity zone: keep all text hierarchy intentional: largest = {메인 자막}, medium = {조회 유도 문구}, small = {채널 핸들} and {에피소드 라벨}; make every Korean character sharp and readable.

[4. STYLE RULES]

- Color palette: follow vivid, high-saturation tones from {컬러 톤}; use a strong contrast pair such as electric red, deep blue, bright yellow, and black or white text accents.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Subject block (left 1/3): {인터뷰이 결} shown in a natural street-interview pose, microphone angled toward the mouth, with clear facial expression, realistic skin detail, fabric texture, and documentary realism.
2. Quote block (right 2/3): {인용 자막} set as the dominant text element in a bold Korean font inside a large high-contrast quoted box, with thick stroke, drop shadow, and a colored underline accent.

4. Background layer: {배경} blurred into city-light bokeh with recognizable Seoul street energy, including hints of crosswalk stripes, café windows, street signage, scooters, and evening or daylight reflections depending on {컬러 톤}.
5. Accent system: {컬러 톤} applied through one sharp highlight color for quote strokes, arrows, sticker shapes, subtitle bars, and small UI elements, while the rest stays grounded in charcoal, off-white, and urban gray.
6. Thumbnail framing: {레이아웃 명세} kept tight and balanced so the subject cutout, quote, topic badge, handle, and supporting hook elements fill the canvas efficiently.
7. Topic cue: {인터뷰 주제} should be visually implied by the subject expression, microphone interaction, and quote emphasis, matching a real street Q&A YouTube format.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold Korean sans-serif such as Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Black for the quote, with crisp edge rendering, thick outline, and size tuned for mobile readability.
- Secondary text handling: channel handle “@streettalk.kr”, “길거리 인터뷰”, “오늘의 질문”, “솔직 답변”, “구독”, and credit text should use Pretendard Medium or SemiBold, arranged as small but readable YouTube-style labels.

- Realistic details: include microphone foam texture, subtle hair strands, jacket folds, street reflection on glass, ambient pedestrians, and natural lens blur so the result feels captured from a real street-interview shoot.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]

[6. MOOD]
Korean street journalism YouTube thumbnail — NYT-style explainer energy meets candid Seoul documentary portrait, with modern Korean creator-channel urgency, bold quotes, and spontaneous real-person reactions.

[7. CRITICAL]

- Thumbnail legibility: all main text must be readable at small mobile size, with no broken Korean characters.
- Interview subject must feel like a real everyday Korean adult, not a celebrity or modeled advertisement pose.
- Keep YouTube-style micro details believable: “@streettalk.kr”, “08:24”, “STREET Q&A”, and “촬영·편집 김PD” should appear as small supporting elements, not as the main message.

- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likenesses

studio:prompts3:ours-509.content:
[INPUT]
- reference_image: {참고 이미지}
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean workplace-experience vlog thumbnail, YouTube click-through design, i2i composition with one preserved hero person, multiple subtitle boxes, and a real part-time-job environment.
Fast, readable entertainment thumbnail for an “알바 체험” video, built to feel like a popular Korean variety-style channel cover captured from an actual busy workday moment.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The main subject occupies the left-center hero area at about 50% of the frame width, cropped from chest to head for strong facial readability.
- Keep {원본 인물} identity-preserving and clearly recognizable; face angle can be 3/4 or front-facing, but the same person must remain the hero.
- Surround the hero with four small caption boxes near the four corners, each box separated from the subject enough to keep the face readable while still feeling dense and clickable.
- Use a bright, energetic Korean YouTube thumbnail layout with layered captions, arrows, sticker-like shapes, reaction marks, and a packed entertainment framing.
- Background should clearly match the work setting of {알바 종류}: include realistic workplace details such as counter surfaces, menu boards, tools, trays, uniforms, shelves, receipts, price tags, steam, lights, or task-specific props that make the job instantly legible.
- Add small YouTube-channel flavor details: a tiny handle label “@alba_vlog”, a red play-button icon shape, a short badge like “VLOG EP.07”, and one click-bait sticker such as “초보 알바생 리얼 후기”.
- Use {알바 종류}, {인물 결}, {레이아웃 명세}, {자막 카피}, {컬러 톤}, {비율} as the content variables driving the render.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero subject area (left-center, mid 50%): {원본 인물} as the dominant focal point, clearly cut and integrated into a lively part-time-job scene, with exaggerated but natural Korean thumbnail energy.
2. Work-context layer: visualize {알바 종류} behind and beside the subject with authentic props and environment cues — for example order slips, gloves, name tag, apron, POS screen, stacked boxes, beverage cups, serving tray, kitchen utensils, store signage, or product displays depending on the job.
3. Expression and pose: render {인물 결} with a comedic variety-thumbnail feel — surprised, awkward, determined, or half-laughing — while keeping the expression readable even at small mobile size.
4. Subtitle box system: place four small yellow caption boxes with black text at the top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right corners, matching {자막 카피} exactly and keeping each box compact and punchy.
5. Main headline band: place one large bottom-center headline from {자막 카피} with the strongest visual weight, using thick black outline, high contrast fill, and extra spacing for quick mobile recognition.
6. YouTube metadata layer: add small but visible details such as “VLOG EP.07”, “알바 체험”, “@alba_vlog”, a small red play icon, a tiny “오늘 첫 출근” sticker, and one arrow or burst shape pointing toward the hero’s reaction.
7. Layout discipline: follow {레이아웃 명세} so the composition reads as a Korean variety-show thumbnail with clear hierarchy, mirrored energy, strong face priority, and layered graphic excitement.
8. Keep the subject’s identity stable across all visible parts of the image; background people may appear only as soft, incidental workplace silhouettes and must never compete with or replace the hero.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: bold Korean thumbnail typography inspired by Pretendard ExtraBold / Noto Sans KR Black, with compact subtitle boxes at around 36–52px feel and the main headline at around 78–110px feel.
- Use thick black outline, high-contrast fill, slight inner shadow, and sticker-like strokes on text for the classic Korean entertainment-thumbnail look; avoid delicate editorial typography.
- Color palette: use the tones from {컬러 톤}, anchored by vivid yellow caption boxes, black text, strong dark outline, red accent badges, white sticker borders, and clean neutral workplace accents.
- Keep yellow caption boxes saturated but not neon, with a slight warm tint; text should be pure black for instant readability.
- Add visual emphasis elements: red arrow, comic burst, small exclamation marks, a tiny shocked emoji-style face, and a circular “리얼 상황” badge, all placed around the subject without covering the eyes.
- Add a subtle soft drop shadow under the hero, headline, sticker badges, and text boxes, about 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity, to separate layers cleanly.
- Preserve real texture in the workplace: fabric apron weave, plastic cup reflections, paper receipt edges, metal counter highlights, product packaging, and natural skin detail.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: 35mm or 50mm equivalent documentary-style framing, as if shot on a Canon EOS R5 with 35mm f/1.8 or Sony A7 IV with 50mm f/1.4, optimized for thumbnail clarity rather than cinematic depth.
- Lighting: bright natural daylight mixed with soft fill, like overcast diffused light from front-left and a mild reflector fill from front-right, keeping facial features crisp and the work area readable.
- Color grade: Korean variety-channel thumbnail grade with clean skin tones, vivid yellows, deep blacks, warm reds, and slightly boosted contrast; preserve natural realism without over-smoothing.
- The image should feel like a polished YouTube cover created from a real workplace snapshot plus graphic subtitle design, with believable objects, task details, and energetic overlay graphics.

[6. MOOD]
Popular Korean entertainment vlog thumbnail — the energetic, fast-read feeling of a high-performing YouTube “알바 체험” channel cover, with a real “첫날 알바 현장” atmosphere, humorous pressure, and friendly chaos.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구를 정확히 표시할 것.
  - "신세경 알바 도전"
  - "실화임?"
  - "이게 더 어렵네"
  - "알바생들 존경"
  - "하루 일당 ?만원"
- Also include small supporting Korean labels where appropriate: "VLOG EP.07", "@alba_vlog", "초보 알바생 리얼 후기", "오늘 첫 출근".
- Preserve {원본 인물} identity and facial likeness; do not change the person into someone else.
- The four corner caption boxes must all be present and match the intended variety-thumbnail layout.
- Keep the subject’s face and expression fully visible and readable; do not obscure the eyes with text, arrows, props, badges, or emojis.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

studio:prompts3:ours-508.content:
[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
유튜브 썸네일용 짤만화 일러스트. 한국 짤만화 채널 특유의 빠르고 직관적인 코믹 리액션을 한 장면에 압축한, 클릭 유도형 와이드 썸네일. {만화 주제}가 즉시 이해되도록 큰 표정, 강한 말풍선, 쇼츠/유튜브 감성의 자막 요소, 채널 핸들, 에피소드 라벨, 액센트 이모지와 도형을 함께 구성한다.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main subject: {만화 주제}를 중심 사건으로 두고, {캐릭터 설정}의 인물 2~3명이 화면 대부분을 차지하게 배치.
- Framing: 캐릭터는 정면 또는 3/4 사선 구도, 풀바디 또는 반신으로 크게 보이게 하며, 말풍선과 대사 박스가 상단·중앙·하단에 겹쳐도 읽히도록 레이어를 명확히 분리.
- Background: 밝은 만화 배경 위에 {배경 소품}을 넣어 상황을 풍부하게 전달한다. 벽시계, 캘린더, 메신저 알림창, 영수증, 회의실 화이트보드, 컵라면, 스마트폰 진동 표시처럼 한국 일상에서 자연스러운 디테일을 추가한다.
- Text placement: 상단에는 {메인 훅}을 굵은 한글 자막으로 크게 넣고, 캐릭터별 말풍선에는 {필수 대사 1}, {필수 대사 2}를 정확히 배치한다. {효과음}은 캐릭터 주변에 짧고 두껍게 흩뿌려 장면의 리액션을 강화한다.
- Layout emphasis: {레이아웃 명세}를 기본 골격으로 삼되, 썸네일 가독성을 위해 얼굴 표정과 손동작이 대사보다 먼저 보이도록 구성. 우측 하단에는 {채널 핸들}, 빨간 재생 버튼 아이콘, 노란 별burst, 두꺼운 화살표, 느낌표, 😱 또는 💥 같은 액센트 이모지/도형을 추가한다.
- Metadata details: 좌측 상단에는 {시리즈 라벨}, 우측 상단에는 {훅 배지}를 스티커처럼 붙인다. 하단 가장자리에는 {크레딧}을 작지만 읽히게 넣어 실제 업로드 썸네일처럼 보이게 한다.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Hero zone: {만화 주제}의 핵심 상황을 화면 중앙에 즉시 인식되게 배치하고, 캐릭터 2~3명의 표정을 과장해 한눈에 감정이 읽히도록 구성.
2) Character block: {캐릭터 설정}에 맞춰 머리는 크게, 몸은 작게, 눈썹과 입 모양은 크게 과장한다. 손과 팔 제스처는 단순하지만 감정이 분명하게 보이게 하고, 셔츠, 후드, 사원증, 넥타이, 앞치마, 슬리퍼, 에코백 등 상황에 맞는 디테일을 넣어 각자의 역할이 보이게 한다.
3) Speech layer: {필수 대사 1}와 {필수 대사 2}를 각각 다른 말풍선 또는 자막 박스로 분리해 캐릭터 옆 또는 위에 붙이고, 말풍선 꼬리는 정확히 화자를 가리키게 처리. 말풍선은 흰색 바탕, 두꺼운 검정 외곽선, 노란 하이라이트 밑줄을 사용해 모바일 화면에서도 읽히게 한다.
4) Effect accents: {효과음}을 작은 한글 효과음으로 주변에 넣고, 빨간 동그라미 표시, 두꺼운 화살표, 번개 스티커, 만화식 땀방울, 속도선, 찌그러진 별 모양, 스마트폰 알림 배지를 곁들여 시선 흐름을 만든다.
5) Thumbnail density: 배경, 텍스트, 캐릭터, 소품이 서로 역할을 나누어 화면을 꽉 채우되, 메인 얼굴과 필수 대사는 가장 높은 대비와 가장 큰 크기로 두어 1초 안에 읽히게 한다.
6) YouTube thumbnail cues: {메인 훅}, {훅 배지}, {시리즈 라벨}, {채널 핸들}이 실제 채널 썸네일 UI처럼 보이도록 배치한다. 클릭 유도형 요소로 빨간 재생 버튼, 구독 스티커, 조회수 느낌의 작은 텍스트 “지금 난리남”, “댓글 폭발” 같은 보조 문구를 자연스럽게 더한다.
7) Format intent: {비율}에 맞는 넓은 썸네일 화면으로 구성하고, 중앙 캐릭터와 상단 제목이 잘리지 않게 안전 영역 안에 배치한다.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: 굵은 한글 손맛 카툰 폰트 느낌, Pretendard ExtraBold 또는 Noto Sans KR Black 계열의 인상, 말풍선 내부는 32~54px급 대형 가독성, 효과음은 더 작고 두껍게. 메인 훅 제목은 흰색 글자에 검정 6~10px 외곽선, 필요 시 노란 하이라이트 박스를 뒤에 깐다.
- Color palette: {컬러 톤} 기반으로 파스텔 핑크 #F8B7C7, 민트 #AEE9D1, 노랑 #F6E27A를 중심에 두고, 외곽선은 진한 검정 #111111으로 강하게. 경고/분노 포인트에는 빨강 #FF3B30, 놀람 포인트에는 파랑 #4DA3FF를 소량 사용한다.
- Border/shadow: 캐릭터와 말풍선 모두 4~8px 굵기의 검정 외곽선, 10~20% 불투명도 그림자와 살짝 어긋난 스티커 드롭섀도를 사용해 레이어가 또렷하게 분리되게 한다.
- Graphic texture: 종이 질감 느낌의 아주 약한 노이즈, 만화 컷 인쇄감, 손그림 선의 미세한 흔들림, 하프톤 점, 작은 잉크 번짐을 넣어 디지털 템플릿이 아니라 실제 짤만화 썸네일처럼 보이게 한다.
- Readability: 모든 큰 텍스트는 모바일에서 읽히도록 두껍고 짧게 구성하며, 말풍선 내부 줄바꿈은 2~3줄 이내로 제한한다. 배경 소품은 상황 설명을 돕되 캐릭터 얼굴과 핵심 대사를 가리지 않게 레이어링한다.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat 2D cartoon illustration, front-facing thumbnail composition, no photographic depth; if perspective is needed, use a subtle 35mm wide editorial framing feel rather than realistic lens blur.
- Lighting: even studio-style flat fill with clean cel-shading, soft edge highlights for separation, small comic shadows under hands, desk props, and speech bubbles to create layered depth.
- Color grade: pastel comic palette with high contrast black outlines, candy pink + mint + warm yellow accents, slightly flattened saturation for meme-thumbnail clarity.
- Rendering: crisp vector-like linework mixed with hand-drawn texture, thick expressive eyebrows, exaggerated mouth shapes, visible cheek blush, sweat marks, motion lines, sticker-style icons, comic halftone bursts, and playful UI-style badges.

[6. MOOD]
Korean meme-comic YouTube thumbnail aesthetic — the fast, punchy readability of popular webtoon reaction panels and community joke images. 웃기지만 현실적인 직장/일상 공감 상황처럼 느껴지며, 과장된 표정과 자막이 동시에 터지는 에너지. 실제 유튜브 피드에서 바로 클릭하고 싶게 만드는 과밀한 재미, 짧은 드라마 한 장면 같은 긴장감, 댓글에서 밈으로 공유될 법한 익살스러움을 담는다.

[7. CRITICAL]
- 반드시 정확히 들어가야 하는 한글 문자열: {필수 대사 1}, {필수 대사 2}.
- 함께 넣을 썸네일 텍스트: {메인 훅}, {훅 배지}, {시리즈 라벨}, {채널 핸들}, {크레딧}.
- 추가 보조 문구는 “지금 난리남”, “댓글 폭발”, “실화냐”, “멘붕주의”처럼 짧고 읽기 쉬운 한국어로만 구성한다.
- 모든 한글 말풍선, 제목, 배지, 라벨, 크레딧은 깨진 글자 없이 선명하게 렌더링한다.
- Character anatomy: 2~3명만 등장, 각 인물의 손가락은 자연스럽게 표현하고 과도하게 늘어나거나 합쳐지지 않게.
- Composition invariant: 유튜브 썸네일 한 장에서 상황, 표정, 대사, 효과음, 채널식 장식 요소가 동시에 읽혀야 함.
- Keep {레이아웃 명세} and {비율} as the guiding layout and aspect-ratio intent while preserving the central {만화 주제}.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals/certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness
