[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
English vocabulary study card sheet in an 8-cell grid, designed for exam prep, TOEIC, daily conversation, and quick Instagram viewing. Make it feel like a real printed study deck page photographed from above: content-rich, practical, and immediately usable for memorization, while still preserving the exact 2x4 card structure.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- The full canvas is a square 2x4 grid with 8 equal vocabulary cards, each card occupying roughly 12.5% of the frame, separated by thin hairline dividers.
- Treat the sheet as a realistic premium study handout on warm paper: visible paper grain, slight ink absorption, tiny print-registration softness, very subtle edge shadow, and a few natural study marks that do not obscure text.
- Each card should feel like a compact vocabulary flashcard: strong hierarchy at the top, useful supporting information below, and enough internal padding for comfortable reading.
- Use {단어 셋} as the overarching vocabulary category context, shown through small category labels and micro headers such as “수능 빈출”, “토익 빈출”, “일상 회화”, or “비즈니스 영어” where appropriate.
- Place {단어 8개} across the grid in balanced reading order, one main word per card, with no card feeling visually heavier than another.
- Apply {컬러 톤} across the entire sheet as the dominant palette, with one accent color used for category chips, check marks, tiny stars, pronunciation icons, and underlines.
- Use {포맷} consistently in every cell so the structure reads instantly as a study sheet, but enrich each cell with realistic learning details: tiny level tag, part-of-speech marker, memory checkbox, one collocation, and a short review note.
- Keep {레이아웃} precise and symmetrical, with uniform margins around the outer edge and equal spacing between cards; maintain {비율} as a square 1:1 study-card sheet.
- Use {타이포} to clearly separate the English headword, IPA, Korean meaning, example sentence, and micro annotations.
- Add small printed-study-page details inside the grid system: card numbers 01–08, tiny “DAY 08” or “REVIEW” labels, subtle dotted guide lines, small progress dots, and brief Korean labels like “뜻 가리기” and “예문 확인”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top line in each card: set the English headword large and bold, centered or slightly left-aligned for quick scanning, with strong legibility and no decorative distortion.
2. Top micro label: include a small card number such as “01”, a category chip such as “수능 빈출” or “토익 빈출”, and a tiny review checkbox or star marker.
3. Second line: place the IPA in a smaller, lighter weight sans-serif directly under the word, paired with a small speaker/pronunciation icon rendered as a simple printed symbol.
4. Third line: place the Korean meaning in a clear serif or serif-like Korean type treatment, slightly larger than the IPA and smaller than the headword.
5. Fourth line: place a very short example sentence under the meaning, compact and classroom-like, with tight line spacing; highlight one target phrase with a soft accent underline.
6. Fifth micro line: add one useful study cue per card, such as “동의어”, “반의어”, “연어”, “시험 포인트”, or “회화 메모”, with very short Korean content.
7. Card treatment: each of the 8 cells should maintain the same internal structure, same padding, and same typographic rhythm so the entire sheet feels consistent.
8. Divider treatment: use thin hairline divider rules between cards, with small accent ticks at selected corners and subtle printed guide marks to make the page feel professionally designed.
9. Background: use a light paper-like base with tactile study-sheet texture, faint fiber speckles, and gentle real-paper shadow rather than a flat digital mockup.
10. Content distribution: spread {단어 8개} evenly so long words do not collide with borders and shorter words still feel visually anchored.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: English headwords in a bold geometric sans-serif such as Pretendard ExtraBold or Noto Sans KR Bold; Korean meanings in Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo Regular; IPA in a small Pretendard Medium or Noto Sans KR Medium.
- Use a refined palette from {컬러 톤}: cream beige, charcoal, and one accent color such as navy or coral; keep saturation moderate and academic while allowing the accent to guide scanning.
- Borders and dividers should be thin 1px hairline rules, with realistic soft print contrast; add light corner ticks, dotted review lines, and small category chips for a richer workbook look.
- Include realistic print details: slightly varied ink density, tiny paper fibers, soft edge curl, faint page shadow, and subtle pencil or highlighter traces that support the study mood.
- Add practical vocabulary-card microcopy in Korean: “오늘의 8단어”, “DAY 08”, “REVIEW”, “체크”, “뜻 가리기”, “예문 확인”, “1분 복습”.
- The design should feel like a premium academic notebook page or magazine-style learning insert, suitable for saving on Instagram and printing for study.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat lay look, simulated with a 50mm standard lens at f/5.6 for even perspective and minimal distortion.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left, with a gentle fill from the right so the paper texture, card dividers, and ink details stay visible without harsh contrast.
- Color grade: warm cream paper base, deep charcoal text, and a single muted navy or coral accent; overall tone should feel like a refined study handout with realistic printed warmth.
- Realism details: slight paper thickness visible at the outer edge, faint desk-tone shadow around the sheet, tiny halftone-like print texture in accent chips, and crisp typography optimized for thumbnail viewing.

[6. MOOD]
Editorial study-sheet design — a polished but practical vocabulary worksheet from a premium academic notebook, with real printed-paper character, exam-prep usefulness, and quick-review Instagram readability.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following Korean strings must appear correctly if shown in the layout or captions: “수능 빈출”, “토익 빈출”, “일상 회화”, “비즈니스 영어”, “여행 영어”, “단어 / 발음 [IPA] / 한글 뜻 / 짧은 예문”, “2x4 그리드 8칸 카드”, “크림 베이지 + 차콜 + 한 가지 액센트 (네이비 또는 코랄) — 학습지 결”, “영문 산세리프 굵은 + 한글 명조 + 작은 IPA 산세리프”.

Designed for internal team sharing, presentation slides, and recap documentation after a sprint or campaign retrospective.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Landscape board composition in a 1536x1024 wide meeting-board layout, with a large centered worksheet canvas and visible meeting-room context such as small sticky tabs, vote dots, hand-drawn arrows, and annotation chips around the main KPT grid.
- Top header area contains {회고 주제} as a bold title band, plus metadata chips for {회고날짜}, {팀명}, {진행자}, {장소}, and {회의코드}.
- Three equal vertical columns for Keep / Problem / Try, each occupying about 28% width, separated by thin 2px divider lines and reinforced by colored vertical strips.
- White paper-like background with subtle off-white tint, faint grid texture, light paper grain, realistic printed ink edges, and crisp infographic spacing.
- Add a practical workshop footer with action owners, next meeting notice, page indicator {페이지표기}, and a small CTA note {마무리문구}.
- {비율} should be reflected as a wide presentation-board layout suitable for screen sharing.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Header band: place {회고 주제} at the top center in a strong editorial heading, with a small subtitle line beneath indicating {프레임}. Add compact metadata labels reading "일시 {회고날짜}", "팀 {팀명}", "진행 {진행자}", "장소 {장소}", and "ID {회의코드}".
2. Main grid: divide the board into three balanced panels labeled Keep, Problem, and Try, each with a colored accent strip, a small icon badge, a count label, and stacked note cards.
3. Keep panel: show {Keep} and {Keep추가} inside rounded white sticky-card blocks with mint accent, small check icons, one circular vote sticker, and a tiny owner tag {Keep담당자}.
4. Problem panel: show {Problem} and {Problem추가} inside rounded white sticky-card blocks with coral accent, alert-dot markers, one red priority chip, and a tiny owner tag {Problem담당자}.
5. Try panel: show {Try} and {Try추가} inside rounded white sticky-card blocks with gold accent, experiment-tag labels, one calendar chip, and a tiny owner tag {Try담당자}.
6. Footer zone: include a realistic meeting summary strip with "다음 액션", "담당", "기한", {다음회의}, {페이지표기}, and {마무리문구}; add small save/share-style micro icons as printed UI decoration.
7. Add subtle handwritten-style annotation snippets in Korean such as "투표 7", "우선순위 높음", "데이터 확인", and "실험 설계" without disrupting the three-column KPT hierarchy.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for all Korean text; title in Bold 40–48px, section labels in SemiBold 22–28px, body text in Regular 18–22px, metadata chips in Medium 13–15px, footer text in Regular 14–16px.
- Color palette: white #FFFFFF, charcoal #2B2F36, mint #6FD6C3 for Keep, coral #F47C74 for Problem, gold #D8B15A for Try, pale gray dividers #E7E9EE, warm paper shadow #DADDE5, soft blue-gray UI chips #EEF3F8.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px charcoal outline on cards, soft drop shadow 0px 6px 18px rgba(43,47,54,0.10), rounded corners 18px, slight paper edge texture on sticky cards.
- Graphic details: use small dots, arrows, tape-like labels, checkbox marks, and vote stickers to make the board feel actively used in a team retrospective.
- Text hierarchy must remain presentation-ready: the KPT labels and the three main notes should be readable first, while metadata, owner tags, and footer details support the scene.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: front-facing orthographic layout, simulated as a flat-lay presentation board with no perspective distortion, equivalent to a 35mm documentary design shot.
- Lighting: soft studio light from upper-left with even fill across the surface, gentle paper shadows under cards and stickers, crisp readable contrast.
- Color grade: clean white + charcoal base with restrained mint/coral/gold accents, slightly cool neutral paper tone and realistic printed-paper texture.
- Rendering: high-resolution editorial infographic, sharp vector-like text treatment combined with tactile paper, sticky-note, marker-dot, and printed worksheet details.

[6. MOOD]
Productivity workshop board — Notion template meets McKinsey-style presentation slide, with the lived-in feel of a real sprint retrospective wall after a focused team discussion.

[7. CRITICAL]

- 화면에 보이는 고정 라벨: "Keep", "Problem", "Try", "일시", "팀", "진행", "장소", "다음 액션", "담당", "기한", "투표 7", "우선순위 높음", "데이터 확인", "실험 설계".
- Layout invariants: three-column KPT structure must be visually equal in width and height, with each card clearly separated and aligned to the same baseline.
- Keep/Problem/Try color coding must remain consistent across label strips, card accents, vote stickers, icon badges, and footer markers.

A warm self-reflection finance dashboard feel with monthly spending summary, category distribution, slide indicator, social handle, save/share cues, and next-month resolution.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main composition: a centered 4-part editorial card-news layout with the monthly total summary occupying the top 28%, the spending chart and budget visuals in the middle 42%, and reflection text blocks plus CTA footer in the lower 30%.
- Background treatment: cream paper-like base with subtle grain, realistic flat-lay desk surface, natural paper fibers, faint pencil marks, tiny receipt edges, sticker tabs, and soft tactile shadows.
- Spacing: readable inner padding, clearly separated blocks, tidy grid alignment, Instagram-readable at thumbnail size, with small realistic UI details such as save/share icons and page dots.
- Use {카드뉴스 제목}, {계정명}, {발행일}, {슬라이드 번호}, {기간·총지출}, {카테고리 분포}, {잘한 것}, {다음 달 다짐}, {저장 CTA}, {해시태그}, {비주얼 결}, {컬러 톤} placeholders.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header area (top 28%): present {카드뉴스 제목} as the main title, {계정명} as a small creator label, {발행일} as a date stamp, and {슬라이드 번호} as a card-news page marker in the upper-right corner.

- Summary block (upper-middle 20%): show total spending and savings as a concise KPI strip with small labels such as “총지출”, “저축”, “전월 대비”, and one number emphasized larger than the rest.
- Chart block (center 22%): render {카테고리 분포} as a donut chart or neat circular breakdown, with labeled segments, percentage tags, tiny won-sign icons, and a small legend on the side.
- Reflection block A (lower-middle 14%): place {잘한 것} in a highlighted note box, using quotation styling, tape sticker detail, and a small memo icon.
- Reflection block B (lower-middle 14%): place {다음 달 다짐} in a second note box, visually balanced with the first and separated by a thin charcoal divider.
- Visual props strip and footer (lower edge 12%): integrate {비주얼 결} as a realistic desk still life or phone finance-app mockup, with a coin jar, notebook, receipts, card slip, pen, page dots, save/share micro icons, {저장 CTA}, and {해시태그}.
- Accent system: apply {컬러 톤} consistently across chart accents, dividers, highlight tags, sticker tabs, icon strokes, and small decorative finance doodles so the whole layout feels like a cohesive MZ budget carousel.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard and Noto Sans KR mix, bold 700–800 for headings, medium 500 for body, numeric figures set slightly larger with tight tracking; quotation notes can use a neat handwritten accent only for emphasis.
- Color palette: cream #F6F1E8, charcoal #2F2F2F, mustard #C89B2C, with soft beige, muted brown, pale olive, and receipt-paper off-white supporting tones from {컬러 톤}.
- Border/shadow: thin charcoal rules, rounded memo cards, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity; keep it editorial and tactile rather than heavy 3D.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean morning challenge card-news style poster for social media story, built like a dawn editorial routine log.
Designed for a motivation/post-check-in use case with a strong progress emphasis, realistic morning-life detail, and readable Korean copy that feels ready to post as a card-news slide.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Tall vertical 1024x1536 card-news canvas with a structured editorial composition: upper headline zone 18%, central visual-and-progress zone 52%, lower log-and-CTA zone 30%.
- Main subject area uses {비주얼 결} as the centerpiece, placed slightly off-center for a human, diary-like feel; text blocks align to a refined editorial grid with visible card-news hierarchy.
- Background should feel like a lived-in pre-dawn interior space: dark navy field, soft window glow, faint curtain silhouette, bedside table edge, notebook paper, coffee mug steam, alarm phone, pen, and warm lamp ambience rendered realistically without overpowering the text.
- Use the requested {컬러 톤} while preserving the navy/amber/off-white editorial palette; make the canvas feel tactile with subtle paper grain, real shadows, small date labels, and routine-tracker details.
- Place {챌린지 종류} as the primary header hook, {진행도} as the most visually dominant metric, {오늘 인증} as a proof strip, and {짧은 후기} as the reflective closing quote.
- Add card-news interface details: slide number “01/05”, page indicator dots, small save/share micro icons, and a bottom CTA strip such as “저장하고 내일 아침 다시 체크”.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Top header band: set {챌린지 종류} in a bold editorial headline, left-aligned or centered depending on balance, with a calm morning-news hierarchy. Include small metadata above or beside it: “MORNING ROUTINE LOG”, “VOL.014”, “2026.05.01 FRI”, and “05:02 AM”.
2. Progress block: display {진행도} as a large numeric or badge-like element, paired with a horizontal progress bar and/or 30 small checkboxes. Make the completion state instantly visible using amber filled checks, off-white labels, and a small caption like “오늘도 기록 완료”.
3. Hero visual block: render {비주얼 결} as a realistic dawn scene or phone-alarm documentary snapshot, not a glossy ad. Include natural objects that belong in a morning challenge: lit phone alarm, folded blanket edge, open habit tracker notebook, pencil, water glass, book page, small towel or yoga band, and warm lamp reflection on the tabletop.
4. Authentication strip: place {오늘 인증} in a compact quote-like container below the hero visual, using monospaced or tightly tracked Korean-friendly text so it feels like a daily log entry. Add a small timestamp label “CHECK-IN 05:02” and a tiny checkmark icon.
5. Reflection block: present {짧은 후기} as a final short paragraph or pull-quote with slightly softer weight, giving the card an introspective, self-motivating finish. Add a small handwritten-style note label such as “오늘의 한 줄”.
6. Footer accent: add a realistic card-news footer with “01 / 05”, five small page indicator dots, tiny icons for 저장 / 공유, and CTA text “내일도 5시에 만나요 · @morning.archive”. Keep the footer integrated with the editorial grid.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard Bold for the main title, Pretendard SemiBold for labels, and Noto Sans KR Regular for body copy; title around 52–64px, labels 20–24px, body 26–32px, progress number 86–120px if space allows.
- Color palette: dark navy #0E1B2E, amber #D89A3B, off-white #F4F1EA, muted gray #8B93A7, and deep charcoal #111318, adapted through {컬러 톤}.
- Border/shadow: subtle 1px divider lines in soft gray, soft drop shadow 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity for the hero container and text cards; add realistic contact shadows beneath notebook, phone, and mug.
- Use clean editorial blocks with practical routine details, compact labels, small tracker marks, date stamps, and tasteful line rules. Decorative elements should feel like printed card-news UI rather than flashy stickers.
- Maintain legibility first: all Korean text should sit on solid or softly translucent surfaces with enough contrast against the dawn background.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: realistic lifestyle capture, 35mm or 50mm full-frame look, f/2.8 to f/4 for mild depth separation, with the option of a phone-screen mockup treated like a product shot.
- Lighting: pre-dawn interior light with soft window light from upper-left at 45°, faint warm practical lamp glow from right, gentle contrast, no harsh specular glare.
- Color grade: deep navy shadows with warm amber highlights, slightly desaturated whites, subtle filmic contrast, morning editorial tone similar to a Kinfolk-style routine spread.
- Texture realism: matte paper card surfaces, slight paper grain, soft fabric texture on bedding or towel, faint condensation on water glass, and believable reflections on the phone screen.
- Composition should support {비율} while keeping the 1024x1536 output and vertical card-news readability.

[6. MOOD]
Premium self-improvement editorial — a quiet Kinfolk magazine spread meets a disciplined morning journal page, with real-life dawn objects, honest routine evidence, and calm momentum.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 표시할 문자열: "미라클모닝 5시 기상 — 또는 30일 운동·독서·금주·물 2L", "DAY 14 / 30 — 큼지막 숫자 + 진행 바 또는 체크박스 30칸", "\"5:02 기상 ✓ 책 30분 ✓ 운동 20분 ✓\"", "\"눈 비비고 일어나면 세상이 조용하다. 그게 좋다.\""
- Additional Korean microcopy may appear if legible: "MORNING ROUTINE LOG", "VOL.014", "2026.05.01 FRI", "CHECK-IN 05:02", "오늘도 기록 완료", "01 / 05", "저장하고 내일 아침 다시 체크", "@morning.archive".
- Keep the overall framing as a tall vertical 1024x1536 card-news slide with a strong progress-first hierarchy and calm dawn mood.
- All Korean text must be clean, correctly spaced, and fully legible; preserve the quote marks and symbols exactly where shown.

Designed as a 필사-style typographic image centered on one quote, enriched with realistic Instagram post details such as a handle, date/location label, hashtags, caption tag, and subtle save/share UI micro icons.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main quote sits slightly above center and occupies about 50–56% of the canvas, with the surrounding paper texture and stationery details visible enough to feel like a real photographed writing card.
- Source line is placed smaller beneath the quote, aligned to the lower-right of the text block for a finished-card structure.
- Add a small top header strip on the paper: {인스타 핸들} at upper-left, {날짜 라벨} and {위치 라벨} at upper-right in tiny neat handwriting or stamped label style.
- Background is {종이 결}, shown as a warm tactile paper surface with visible fibers, slight waviness, faint pressure marks, and natural uneven tone.
- Include nearby realistic stationery details: {필기구} partially visible near an edge, soft ink-test marks, a tiny paper clip or washi tape fragment, and {장식} as a small accent integrated with the handwritten card.
- Bottom area includes Instagram-card micro details: {캡션}, {해시태그}, and tiny save/share/comment icon marks drawn like simple line UI symbols, kept secondary to the quote.
- Use {글귀}, {출처}, {필기구}, {종이 결}, {장식}, {컬러 톤}, {인스타 핸들}, {날짜 라벨}, {위치 라벨}, {캡션}, {해시태그} placeholders naturally in the layout.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Quote block (center focus): Render {글귀} in expressive Korean handwriting with relaxed stroke rhythm, slightly varied line thickness, authentic pen pressure, and balanced spacing so the text feels handwritten rather than typeset.
- Source line (lower-right of quote block): Place {출처} in smaller, lighter handwritten text, separated from the quote by a modest gap for clear hierarchy.
- Instagram header: Place {인스타 핸들} as a small profile-style line with a tiny circular avatar doodle, then place {날짜 라벨} and {위치 라벨} as compact labels resembling a real saved-feed card.
- Writing material cues: Depict the mark quality of {필기구} accurately—ink bleed for brush pen, crisp nib edges for fountain pen, or softer pigment texture for colored pencil / marker.
- Paper field: Show {종이 결} across the entire square, with fibers, tooth, slight shadow at paper edges, soft creases, and gentle off-white variation visible around the lettering.
- Accent detail: Add {장식} as an editorial stationery ornament, such as a leaf sketch, dot doodle, pressed-flower sticker, or a small tape strip, positioned asymmetrically with handmade charm.
- Footer micro content: Render {캡션} and {해시태그} as small readable handwriting or neat printed microtext, accompanied by simple save/share/comment icons and a tiny page-dot indicator.
- Color balance: Apply {컬러 톤} so the image stays cohesive with charcoal ink, warm paper, and one restrained accent color appearing in the decoration, label, or icon details.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: hand-lettered Korean calligraphy look, with a hybrid of brush-calligraphy and modern editorial handwriting; quote at large size equivalent to 62–78 px feel, source at 18–24 px feel, header/footer microtext at 12–16 px feel.
- Use {컬러 톤} exactly as the palette direction: white + black + one accent tone such as sage green, muted rose, or gold, with paper-friendly contrast.
- Border/shadow: use a realistic paper-edge shadow if the sheet is visible, around 2–4px edge depth, 8px blur, 10–16% opacity, matching a top-down stationery photograph.
- Micro UI marks should look hand-drawn or lightly printed, not like a perfect app screenshot; keep them integrated into the physical paper-card aesthetic.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: top-down flat lay look, simulated with a 50mm lens at f/4 for a natural stationery-photo perspective.
- Lighting: soft window light from upper-left at about 45°, with a very mild fill from lower-right; keep shadows feathered and realistic, no harsh hotspots.
- Color grade: warm ivory paper, charcoal black ink, and one muted accent color, with slightly desaturated editorial tones and gentle contrast.
- Texture realism: visible paper tooth, ink pooling at stroke endings, small pressure variations, subtle dust specks, and natural handmade imperfections.

[6. MOOD]
Quiet Korean stationery editorial — like a saved Instagram 필사 post from a poetry-loving desk, with a Yun Dong-ju / Jeong Ho-seung book-page atmosphere and the warmth of a real handwritten note.

[7. CRITICAL]
- 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열: {글귀}, {출처}, {인스타 핸들}, {날짜 라벨}, {위치 라벨}, {캡션}, {해시태그}.
- 한글은 깨지지 않고 자연스럽게 읽혀야 하며, 획이 장식 기호처럼 변형되면 안 된다.
- 인스타그램 카드 요소는 보조 정보로만 배치하고, 주인공은 하나의 큰 필사 글귀여야 한다.
- 작은 아이콘은 저장, 공유, 댓글을 암시하는 단순 선 아이콘으로 표현하되, 실제 앱 화면 캡처처럼 보이지 않게 한다.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]

7) Format fit: keep the entire design locked to {비율}, with square-safe spacing and no edge-cut text.

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean GoodNotes digital diary page template, iPad 4:3 planner layout for weekly scheduling, habit tracking, and note-taking.
Designed as an Instagram-friendly diary-decorating planner sheet with a realistic hand-drawn digital stationery feel, suitable for use as a downloadable tablet planner page.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Page format: landscape 4:3 canvas with an iPad-notebook look, visible digital paper sheet edges, soft screen-like shadow, and a clear hierarchy suitable for {페이지 종류}.
- Main layout: organize the page as {레이아웃}, with the schedule area taking roughly 62% of the width and the notes/todo area taking the remaining 38%.
- Background treatment: warm paper-like cream base with subtle off-white grain, faint digital paper fiber, and crisp vector-like ruled lines for a practical planning surface.
- Realistic planner content: include a dated weekly header for {주간 날짜}, a small month marker for {월 표시}, weekday labels, tiny weather/mood check circles, and a few light handwritten sample notes that demonstrate use without filling every writing line.
- Spacing and framing: use consistent outer padding, aligned grid spacing, rounded section cards, small index tabs, and enough writable room for schedule entries, memos, and checklist items.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header zone (top 12%): title area left-aligned for {페이지 종류}, showing the rendered title “굿노트 위클리”, the week range “{주간 날짜}”, and a small monthly badge “{월 표시}”. Place a neat decorative accent cluster on the right using {장식}.
- Schedule column: build the time planner using {시간 블록}, with evenly spaced horizontal rows, 30-minute hairline sub-dividers, and small Korean weekday/date labels such as “5/4 MON”, “5/5 TUE”, “5/6 WED”.
- Right notes/todo panel: stack {오른쪽 섹션} as separate rounded boxes with checkboxes, dot bullets, tiny sticky-note shapes, and a compact habit tracker grid.
- Functional micro content: add a mini habit tracker labeled “HABIT”, a water tracker labeled “WATER”, a small priority list labeled “TOP 3”, and a memo area labeled “MEMO”, using practical GoodNotes-style planner markings.
- Decorative micro-elements: add tiny hand-drawn icons and handwritten sample marks from {장식} near headings, tabs, and sticker corners; keep the writing grid readable and usable.
- Palette application: render the overall page in {컬러 톤}, applying the accent color to section labels, mini stickers, tabs, checkboxes, date badges, and key dividers.
- Typography treatment: use {타이포} for headings and labels, with a legible handwritten-note rhythm and consistent digital pen stroke weight across the page.
- Footer details: include a small page footer with “{하단 문구}”, a page indicator “p. 07”, and subtle punch-hole or binder-ring marks along the far left edge for a digital notebook impression.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard and Noto Sans KR as the main clean sans-serif base, paired with a hand-drawn note style for small captions; headings around 28–34 px, labels around 16–20 px, body lines around 13–15 px.
- Color palette: cream beige, charcoal gray, soft lavender or sage accent, and muted warm white paper tones from {컬러 톤}; use dark text for readable tablet-planner contrast.
- Border/shadow: thin 1px rules, rounded section cards, soft sticker shadows, and a very soft 2px drop shadow at 10% opacity to suggest an iPad screen overlay without looking glossy.
- Line quality: crisp ruled lines and hairline grids should feel like a real PDF planner template imported into GoodNotes, with slightly imperfect hand-drawn icons for warmth.
- Decorative balance: include realistic diary-deco details such as washi tape strips, mini check stickers, pen-drawn arrows, small stars, and coffee/moon icons while preserving the function of the planner.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: crisp top-down digital mockup look, equivalent to a 50mm flat-lay product shot with an orthographic presentation, no perspective distortion.
- Lighting: even diffused studio light from above-left with a gentle fill from the opposite side, keeping the page surface evenly readable and free of harsh glare.
- Color grade: cream beige + charcoal + muted lavender/sage, with low saturation and clean contrast for a stationery-app aesthetic.

[6. MOOD]
Clean iPad planner editorial — similar to a polished GoodNotes / Notability showcase on Pinterest and Instagram, with hand-finished diary decoration energy, practical study-planner details, and cozy Korean digital stationery charm.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the rendered image must include these strings exactly as intended when text is present: “굿노트 위클리”, “06:00”, “23:00”, “THIS WEEK”, “TO DO”, “MEMO”, “HABIT”, “WATER”.
- Date realism: include Korean-friendly planner labels such as “2026.05”, “5/4 MON”, “5/5 TUE”, “오늘의 할 일”, “운동”, “독서”, and “물 마시기” as small readable text.
- Layout invariants: preserve a 4:3 landscape planner page, left schedule + right memo structure, evenly spaced time rows, and decorative icons placed around headings, tabs, and corners.
- The page must feel editable, organized, and stationery-like, not like a poster or ad banner.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Broken Korean characters
- Fake official seals or certifications
- Celebrity composites or recognizable public figures
- Overly glossy AI-smooth surfaces

[1. PURPOSE]
1-page printable habit tracker poster for Korean self-care use, designed as an A4 vertical planner sheet with a practical daily check-off system, realistic printed stationery details, and enough structure to feel like an actual desk planner page.
66-day challenge format with strong legibility, print-first composition, and social-media-ready editorial polish.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main page fills the full portrait frame with a structured planner layout: title band at the top, challenge metadata and motivation quote beneath, then a large 5-row by 66-day grid occupying most of the page.
- {챌린지 종류} should be placed in the top header area as the primary title, centered and visually dominant, with a small Korean label above it such as “HABIT TRACKER · 66 DAYS”.
- Add realistic planner micro-details around the header: “START ____ / END ____”, “NAME ____”, “VOL.066”, and a tiny print code like “PRINTABLE A4 · DAILY CHECK”.
- {동기부여 카피} sits directly under the header in a smaller emphasis line, aligned to the title block and framed by a fine accent rule.
- The main body uses {격자 구조} with clearly separated day columns and habit rows, including tiny day numbers 01–66 along the top and small weekly section markers.
- {습관 항목 5개} labels the left side of the grid with compact row headers, each aligned to a corresponding habit row, with small check icons or numbered bullets integrated into the label column.
- Use {비율} as the design proportion reference for the vertical A4-style layout, keeping the printable sheet visually centered in the 1024x1536 frame.
- Background should be warm off-white paper with believable matte paper fiber, faint print ink density variation, tiny crop marks, and subtle desk-scanner realism.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header band (top 12–15%): set {챌린지 종류} in a bold centered title block with a crisp divider line below; include small supporting Korean/English stationery labels such as “66-DAY ROUTINE LOG”, “VOL.066”, and “매일 한 칸”.
- Subtitle and metadata line (upper-middle 8%): place {동기부여 카피} in quotation marks as a smaller supporting line, centered under the title; add “시작일 ____”, “완료일 ____”, and “작성자 ____” fields in fine type.
- Grid body (middle 65–70%): render {격자 구조} as a precise calendar-style matrix, with 66 vertical day slots and exactly 5 horizontal habit rows; every cell must remain large enough for visible pen check marks, circles, or color fills after printing.
- Day-number strip: include day numbers 01 through 66 across the top of the grid, with every 7th day visually grouped; add small Korean weekly labels such as “1주차”, “2주차”, “3주차” up to the final week where space allows.
- Habit labels (left column): render {습관 항목 5개} as numbered row labels, aligned left with consistent line height and practical planner spacing; include small memo ticks beside each row.
- Divider emphasis: every Sunday column should use a thicker vertical rule than the other columns, creating a visible weekly rhythm; small accent dots may mark weekly milestones at days 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63, and 66.
- Footer zone (bottom 6–8%): include a usable notes and reflection area with printed Korean labels such as “이번 주 기록”, “느낀 점”, “보상”, “다음 목표”, plus a small completion progress bar labeled “완료율 ____%”.
- Add subtle realistic print features: tiny page number “PAGE 01”, a narrow barcode-like reference block labeled “HABIT-066”, and small scissors/crop guide marks near the lower edge.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use {타이포}; if unspecified, use Pretendard Bold for the main header, Pretendard SemiBold for subtitles and section labels, Pretendard Regular for grid labels and microcopy; title size large and page-dominant, body text compact but highly legible.
- Color palette: use {컬러 톤} while preserving cream paper #F4F0E6, charcoal #2B2B2B, forest green #2F5D50 or coral #D96B5F as the main accent; accent color appears in divider rules, weekly dots, section tags, and progress markers.
- Border/shadow: print-safe outer frame in charcoal with subtle paper edge shadow, slightly rounded paper corners, and gentle top-down contact shadow so the sheet feels physically printed.
- Planner detailing: use fine rules, small labels, date blanks, page code, check icons, weekly milestone dots, and note boxes to make the design content-rich while keeping the grid practical for handwriting.
- The final image should look like a professionally designed Korean printable planner sheet photographed or scanned for a stationery catalog, not a blank template.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: flat graphic layout, top-down editorial poster look as if photographed with a 50mm lens at f/8 for a perfectly even, distortion-free page capture.
- Lighting: soft diffuse daylight from above, neutral and shadow-light, with natural paper texture, faint edge shadow, and realistic printed ink on matte stationery paper.
- Color grade: warm cream paper base with crisp charcoal text and one muted accent tone, calibrated for clean CMYK-friendly printing.
- Physical realism: slight paper tooth, fine toner/ink edges, subtle off-white tonal variation, and precise vector-like grid lines that remain readable at poster size.

[6. MOOD]
Calm Korean stationery editorial — Muji notebook + Kinfolk planner spread feel, disciplined, useful, warm, and motivating, with the richness of a real printable self-care tracker sold in a lifestyle stationery shop.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following verbatim Korean strings must appear correctly in the rendered image:
  - 66일 습관 챌린지 — 또는 30일 운동·물 2L·금연·기상·독서
  - 01 6시 기상 / 02 운동 30분 / 03 물 2L / 04 책 30분 / 05 일기
  - 가로 30/66일 + 세로 5항목 — 일자별 체크박스, 일요일은 굵은 라인 강조
  - "66일이면 습관이 된다 — 한 칸씩 채우자"
- Additional Korean microcopy may appear as realistic planner details: “START ____”, “END ____”, “작성자 ____”, “이번 주 기록”, “느낀 점”, “보상”, “다음 목표”, “완료율 ____%”, “매일 한 칸”, “PAGE 01”.
- Layout invariants: exactly 5 habit rows, day grid spanning 66 days, clearly visible checkbox cells, day numbers 01–66, and thicker Sunday separators.
- Print-readability: all Korean text must be crisp, evenly spaced, and fully contained within the printable page area.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]
- language: Korean

[1. PURPOSE]
YouTube thumbnail for a company promo video, SaaS keynote-style marketing visual built for click-through without feeling like a flat banner ad.
Designed for a corporate product launch thumbnail with a realistic laptop mockup, detailed UI screen, smiling user portrait, bold Korean title text, channel identity cues, and small launch-video metadata elements.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main hero composition: the laptop mockup and UI screen occupy about 52% of the frame on the left-center, while the smiling person portrait fills the right 28% as a cropped half-body cutout with realistic skin texture, natural hair detail, and studio-lit clothing folds.
- Header text zone: {키 메시지} sits large in the upper-left, covering roughly 18% of the width, with strong hierarchy, punchy Korean line breaks, and a small accent shape or emoji-like marker such as “▶” or “✨” beside the first line.
- Brand/product cue: {회사·제품} appears as a smaller supporting label near the top or beside the laptop UI, visually tied to the product interface; add a tiny channel handle line such as “@company_official” and a compact label “PRODUCT TOUR 2026”.
- CTA treatment: {CTA 뱃지} is a compact pill badge placed near the lower-right of the headline cluster, paired with a small arrow chip reading “바로가기” and a subtle click-cursor graphic to create YouTube thumbnail urgency.
- Background treatment: SaaS conference keynote look on a white base with deep navy panels, realistic soft shadows, lime accent strokes, small UI widgets, floating metric cards, and a faint stage-screen grid that makes the launch setting feel real and content-rich.
- Thumbnail details: include a small red play icon, a tiny “3:24” video-duration tag near a corner, a short micro-caption like “실제 사용 화면 공개”, and 1–2 compact view-bait callouts such as “오늘 공개” or “신규 업데이트”.
- Framing direction: keep all key elements angled slightly toward the center so the thumbnail reads instantly at small size while still feeling like a polished promo-video cover.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Background layer: build a crisp white foundation with deep navy stage blocks, thin UI divider lines, subtle lime accent lines, small chart fragments, tiny cursor marks, and a soft tabletop or keynote-screen surface feel.
2. Product hero layer: place a modern laptop mockup prominently, showing a catalog-builder interface on its screen with sharp rectangular panels, product cards, thumbnail images, price rows, left sidebar navigation, status chips, and visible content hierarchy.
3. UI content layer: add realistic SaaS details on and around the laptop, such as “상품 관리”, “카탈로그 미리보기”, “주문 링크”, small graph cards, toggle buttons, and a highlighted lime outline around the main feature area.
4. Human support layer: add a friendly smiling person cutout near the product, lit evenly and cropped tightly so the face reads clearly at thumbnail size; the person may gesture toward the laptop or hold a small tablet/phone showing a matching product preview.
5. Message layer: render {키 메시지} as the largest typographic block, bold and compact, with strong line breaks that keep the phrase readable within one glance; add a tiny upper kicker like “회사 홍보 영상” or “런칭 데모” above it.
6. Brand label layer: position {회사·제품} as a smaller contextual line, aligned with the UI or header area, acting as a supporting identity cue rather than a competing headline; include a small “OFFICIAL” or “NEW” label nearby.
7. CTA layer: place {CTA 뱃지} as a noticeable badge button with high contrast, supported by the exact text “바로가기”, a small arrow, and a cursor pointer to imply immediate action.
8. YouTube metadata layer: add a small channel handle “@brand_channel”, a tiny duration chip “3:24”, a red play icon, and a compact teaser line “실제 화면으로 확인” near the bottom edge.
9. Finishing layer: apply conference-keynote polish—realistic shadows, controlled contrast, crisp UI edges, layered typography, and precise spacing—so the whole composition feels like a finished SaaS product-launch thumbnail.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use {타이포} for the main headline when provided; otherwise use Pretendard ExtraBold for the main headline, with smaller English support text in Inter or Pretendard Medium; headline size should dominate the frame, with tight line spacing and sharp edges.
- Color palette: use {컬러 톤} as the primary direction when provided; otherwise use white #FFFFFF, deep navy #0B1F3A, lime accent #C7F000, light gray #E8EDF3, optional dark slate #1E2A3A for contrast.
- Visual texture: reflect {비주얼 결} through the finish of the thumbnail, adding realistic laptop reflections, fabric detail, UI micro-shadows, tiny labels, and stage-screen depth without sacrificing legibility.
- Border/shadow: soft realistic shadow under the laptop mockup, about 6px y-offset, 18px blur, 14% opacity; CTA badge with a subtle 1px outline and a crisp pressed-button feel.
- Graphic accents: use lime arrows, rounded rectangles, small interface chips, play-icon marker, sticker-like “NEW” tag, and a tasteful circular spotlight behind the portrait to add depth and click appeal.
- Layout ratio: maintain {비율} when provided and keep the 1536x1024 thumbnail composition optimized for YouTube preview scale.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: polished corporate product-photo framing, equivalent to a 35mm lens at f/4 with a straight-on promotional layout; crisp UI edges and thumbnail-friendly readability.
- Lighting: studio softbox key from upper-left at about 45°, gentle fill from the front-right, slight controlled rim on the person cutout to separate them from the white background.
- Color grade: clean cool corporate grade with white + deep navy + lime accents, slight contrast boost, natural skin tones, realistic laptop highlights, and refined SaaS launch-video polish.

[6. MOOD]
SaaS conference keynote thumbnail — polished product launch cover with the clarity and hierarchy of a Webflow / Notion-style presentation slide, plus YouTube-native energy from bold Korean text, CTA badge, channel handle, play icon, and demo-screen details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following strings must appear exactly as written: “3분 만에 내 가게 카탈로그”, “무료 체험”, “바로가기”.
- Render {키 메시지}, {회사·제품}, and {CTA 뱃지} clearly as primary thumbnail text elements, preserving the exact placeholder-provided Korean when supplied.
- Include realistic YouTube thumbnail details: “@brand_channel”, “PRODUCT TOUR 2026”, “3:24”, “실제 사용 화면 공개”, and a small red play icon.
- Keep the composition precisely thumbnail-readable: laptop mockup, detailed UI screen, bold Korean title, CTA badge, and smiling person must all remain clearly visible and balanced.
- Maintain a SaaS keynote feel with strong hierarchy, and keep the CTA supportive rather than larger than the main message.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
One-page corporate report infographic for executives, built as a realistic vertical A4-style strategy summary sheet. Designed to communicate KPI performance, chart evidence, and a single action-driving insight in 5 seconds while looking like a printed internal board-report page from a real company briefing pack.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Poster fills the full vertical frame like an A4 consulting deck page, with a strong top headline band, KPI strip below it, charts in a structured middle section, and a closing insight box near the lower third.
- Main subject area should feel like a polished business report page on premium off-white paper, with precise alignment, thin dividers, section labels, small metadata, chart legends, source notes, and realistic print detail.
- Use {보고 주제} as the headline theme, {KPI 3개} for the metric strip, {차트 종류} for the chart set, {인사이트 한 줄} for the final takeaway, {컬러 톤} for palette direction, {타이포} for typography direction, and {비율} for page framing.
- Add realistic report-page content around the core infographic: document code, date label, department credit, page number, confidentiality tag, quarter marker, source footnote, tiny legend chips, annotation arrows, and a small executive-summary note block.
- The design should feel content-rich and boardroom-ready, with enough labels and microcopy to resemble an actual KPI report rather than a template mockup.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Top header band (top 14%): Set {보고 주제} as the main title in a strong executive-report style, centered or slightly left-aligned. Add compact report metadata such as 'EXECUTIVE KPI REPORT', '2026년 5월호', 'VOL. 247', '작성: 전략기획팀', '기밀 / 내부 검토용', and a small document ID like 'RPT-KR-05-247'. Place a thin separation line beneath the header and include a tiny right-aligned date stamp.
- KPI strip (upper-mid 18%): Place {KPI 3개} as three large numeric blocks in a row, each with a bold number, short Korean label, subtle directional arrow or delta indicator, period comparison text such as '전월 대비', '목표 대비', 'YoY', and a tiny sparkline or progress gauge inside each card. Use consistent spacing and identical card widths.
- Chart zone A (mid-left 24%): Render the first chart from {차트 종류} as a crisp vector-style business chart with clear axes, gridlines, data labels, legend chips, and one highlighted annotation callout such as '주요 변곡점' or '목표선 상회'.
- Chart zone B (mid-right 24%): Render the second chart from {차트 종류} with the same visual system, aligned to the same baseline and scale logic so the page feels like one coherent report. Add a small comparison caption like '지역별 / 채널별 기여도' and a legend row with 2–3 colored series labels.
- Chart zone C (lower-mid 16%): Render the third chart from {차트 종류} as a compact supporting visualization with readable labels, value tags, and a small table-like summary row beneath it, including Korean microcopy such as '상위 항목', '리스크', '기회 요인'.
- Insight box (bottom 12%): Place {인사이트 한 줄} in a highlighted quotation-style callout with a thin border and light accent background. Add a small label above it reading '핵심 인사이트' and a final action cue below it such as '다음 회의 안건: 우선순위 재정렬 및 실행 담당 확정'.
- Footer strip: Include realistic report footer elements: '자료: 내부 CRM·ERP 집계, 2026.05 기준', 'p.01 / Executive Summary', a tiny page marker, and a small non-official company-style text mark such as 'Strategy Planning Office'.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Use Pretendard Bold for the main headline, Pretendard SemiBold for KPI labels, and a refined serif like Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo for the insight quote; headline about 42–56 px, KPI numbers about 34–44 px, labels about 16–20 px, metadata and footnotes about 9–12 px. Follow {타이포} while maintaining an executive Korean report hierarchy.
- Color palette: Follow {컬러 톤} with an off-white or pure white base (#FFFFFF or #F7F7F4), charcoal text (#222222 / #2B2B2B), and one accent color such as navy (#163A63) or mustard (#C89B2C) used for emphasis, arrows, chart highlights, date chips, and callout rules.
- Border/shadow: Use hairline dividers, 1–2 px rules, subtle card shadows (0 y-offset, 6–10 px blur, 8–12% opacity), light table ruling, and fine chart gridlines so the page stays flat, editorial, and professional rather than glossy.
- Data realism: Use plausible business-chart values, visible tick marks, axis labels, deltas, legends, and footnotes. Chart marks should look like carefully designed consulting-deck graphics, not abstract decorative shapes.
- Paper detail: Add faint premium paper grain, tiny print-registration softness, and slight ink density variation so the image feels like a real photographed report sheet while all key text remains readable.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: Clean front-on document-poster render, as if photographed with a 50mm lens at f/8 for flatness and clarity, no perspective distortion.
- Lighting: Even studio lighting with soft overhead diffusion, gentle natural paper shadow at the page edge, and consistent brightness across the entire report sheet.
- Color grade: Crisp white, charcoal, and restrained accent color grading with a consulting-deck presentation tone, low saturation, high readability.
- Rendering finish: High-resolution printed-report realism, sharp vector charts, precise Korean typography, realistic toner/ink edges, and subtle tactile paper texture.

[6. MOOD]
Premium strategy-consulting report page — McKinsey / BCG presentation aesthetic with a disciplined editorial infographic feel, but with the density and credibility of a real internal executive KPI briefing.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문구: {보고 주제}, {KPI 3개}, {차트 종류}, {인사이트 한 줄}.
- 반드시 선명하게 들어갈 보조 문구: 'EXECUTIVE KPI REPORT', '2026년 5월호', 'VOL. 247', '작성: 전략기획팀', '기밀 / 내부 검토용', '자료: 내부 CRM·ERP 집계', 'p.01 / Executive Summary', '핵심 인사이트'.
- All chart labels, KPI numbers, legends, captions, metadata, source notes, and the insight sentence must be cleanly typeset and fully readable.
- Keep the composition as a single-page executive summary with one headline, one KPI row, three charts, one insight callout, realistic footer metadata, and board-report microcopy.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]

- output_size: 1536x1024

[1. PURPOSE]
Korean internal company announcement event card for Slack/Teams-style communication. Create a realistic, content-rich corporate notice card with clear hierarchy, useful micro-details, and workplace communication context, suitable for HR announcements, internal events, policy updates, and team-wide reminders.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Canvas is a 1536x1024 landscape card, with a left-to-right reading flow, polished editorial spacing, and a practical in-app announcement feel.
- Main title block occupies the upper-left 40% of the frame, with supporting details stacked beneath using precise alignment and readable line lengths.
- Visual cluster sits on the right 28–34% of the frame as a realistic internal event graphic area: mini calendar card, notification panel, illustrated laptop/coffee/calendar items, RSVP chip, and small employee avatar dots.
- Use {공지 종류}, {제목}, {본문}, {비주얼}, {컬러 톤}, {발신자}, {비율} as the editable content elements.
- Background is a refined corporate surface with subtle paper grain, soft matte gradient, faint grid hints, and layered UI-card depth that still keeps the announcement readable.
- Add believable corporate metadata: small notice ID such as “NOTICE-2026-05”, date label “2026.05.01”, channel tag “#사내공지”, and tiny status chip “필독” or “D-7” where appropriate.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Header zone: place {공지 종류} as a small category label at the top-left, set in a clear pill or tag style with strong contrast and tight padding. Nearby, add small Korean UI metadata such as “사내 공지”, “VOL.024”, “2026.05.01”, and “#HR뉴스”.
2) Title zone: render {제목} directly below as the dominant headline, large and bold, occupying roughly 2 lines max with crisp Korean letterforms and natural headline tracking.
3) Body zone: place {본문} beneath the title in smaller, readable lines with clear line spacing. Add subtle supporting rows if useful: “대상: 전 임직원”, “장소: 본사 라운지 / 온라인”, “확인 기한: 5월 10일(금)” as small secondary information blocks.
4) Visual zone: build {비주얼} on the right side as a polished illustration cluster or semi-realistic corporate graphic, integrating a calendar tile, document card, chat bubble, laptop screen, coffee cup, small badge, or employee avatar stack. Include tiny labels like “일정 저장”, “참여 신청”, “알림 설정”, and “문의 HR팀”.
5) Footer zone: set {발신자} aligned near the lower-left or lower-right edge as a subtle sender line, with an adjacent contact row such as “문의: people@company.co.kr” and a compact CTA button reading “자세히 보기”.
6) Format control: preserve {비율} as a landscape internal memo layout with rectangular card proportions, optimized for sharing inside Slack/Teams message threads rather than tall poster framing.
7) Extra workplace details: include a small reaction bar at the bottom such as “👍 24   💬 8   저장”, a page/card marker like “01 / 01”, and a tiny QR-placeholder box or calendar icon area only if it fits the composition naturally.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for the entire card; headline weight 700–800, body weight 400–500, sender weight 500; title size should feel around 44–60px equivalent, body around 22–28px equivalent, metadata around 14–18px equivalent.
- Color palette: white #FFFFFF, charcoal #2B2F36, soft gray #E9EDF2, and {컬러 톤} as the accent direction; use the accent for category chips, CTA buttons, small icons, calendar highlights, and divider lines.
- Border/shadow: use a subtle 1px divider or card outline with soft drop shadow 0px 6px 18px at 12–15% opacity; add layered cards, soft interface panels, and small tactile shadows for realistic depth.
- UI details: include rounded rectangles, notification badges, tiny icon buttons, micro dividers, avatar circles, and compact information chips that make the card feel like a real workplace announcement asset.
- Text rendering: all Korean text must be sharp, aligned to a consistent grid, and visually plausible as a company communication design.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: clean graphic design presentation, simulated as a straight-on 50mm product-style composition, flat and distortion-free, as if photographed or exported from a high-quality corporate design mockup.
- Lighting: soft studio daylight feel from upper-left with even fill across the surface, gentle card shadows, and realistic separation between layered panels.
- Color grade: Slack/Teams-like corporate interface palette, crisp white base with charcoal text and one professional brand accent matching {컬러 톤}.
- Materials: matte digital card surface, soft paper-like grain, subtle UI panel translucency, and refined vector icons mixed with semi-realistic office illustration details.

[6. MOOD]
Premium internal workplace notice — modern Slack announcement card aesthetic with a polished Notion/Teams communication panel finish, realistic company event context, friendly HR tone, and enough visual information to feel like an actual announcement shared by a corporate team.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 아래 문구가 정확히 보여야 함: {공지 종류}, {제목}, {본문}, {발신자}
- Additional Korean microcopy may appear and should be clean and legible, for example: “사내 공지”, “NOTICE-2026-05”, “참여 신청”, “일정 저장”, “문의 HR팀”, “자세히 보기”, “대상: 전 임직원”.
- Layout invariants: title hierarchy must be obvious at a glance, text must remain crisp and fully legible, and the right-side visual must stay secondary to the announcement text.
- Keep the card office-appropriate, message-app friendly, and realistic as an internal company communication asset.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters

[INPUT]
- language: Korean
- output_size: 1024x1536

[1. PURPOSE]
신입 OJT·온보딩 가이드 표지, 세로형 사내 문서 커버, 내부 배포용 편집 디자인.
회사 첫인상과 실무 안내를 한 장에 전달하는 환영형 표지이며, 실제 인쇄된 핸드북 첫 장처럼 버전 정보, 발행일, 담당 조직, 목차 단서가 함께 보이는 현실적인 커버.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Overall layout: centered editorial cover with a strong title block in the upper 28%, hero visual in the middle 42%, and onboarding scope band in the lower 18%.
- Main subject placement: {대표 비주얼} anchored slightly right of center, with a structured left-side column for title hierarchy, welcome metadata, and quick-start checklist.
- Background treatment: warm white base with tactile off-white paper texture, faint paper fibers, subtle geometric shapes, thin line accents, small tab markers, and brand-derived color chips in {컬러 톤}.
- Spacing and framing: A4-style document grid with realistic print-safe margins, visible baseline rhythm, small registration-style alignment marks, and a polished internal handbook layout.
- Text hierarchy: {회사·직무} as the primary context line, {환영 메시지} as the main headline, {가이드 범위} as the supporting scope line.
- Add real guide-cover details: include a small issue/version label such as "ONBOARDING GUIDE VOL.03", date label "2026.05", document code "HR-OJT-2026-05", and a small QR-code/barcode-style access area labeled "사내 포털 바로가기".

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
- Header zone (top 18%): place the main headline {환영 메시지} in bold sans-serif, large and left-aligned, with a smaller context line {회사·직무} beneath it; add a compact cover kicker "NEW MEMBER HANDBOOK" and date chip "2026년 5월 업데이트".
- Brand/identity zone (upper-mid 12%): integrate a professional company identity area using {대표 비주얼} with abstract graphic support, a small department credit line "People Team · Learning Experience", and tiny spine-style vertical text "신입 OJT·온보딩 가이드 / 내부 배포용" along one side.
- Hero visual zone (mid 42%): show {대표 비주얼} as the dominant visual element, styled like a polished internal handbook cover—either a warm portrait cutout, a realistic office desk/object scene, or an editorial illustration—paired with line graphics, onboarding timeline pins, sticky-note shapes, ID-card cues, laptop/calendar fragments, and soft shadow layering.
- Scope band (lower 16%): display {가이드 범위} in a neat horizontal or stacked module format, with clear separation between W1, W2, W3, and W4; each module should have a small icon cue, short label, and progress-dot detail.
- Footer zone (bottom 12%): include practical document footer information: "담당: People Team", "문의: onboarding@company.co.kr", "Ver. 1.2", page marker "COVER / 00", and a small QR-code/barcode-style box without claiming official certification.
- Additional realistic cover copy: add 2–3 short Korean blurbs such as "첫 주 체크리스트", "계정·도구 설정", "멘토와 함께 시작하기" in small editorial callouts.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard bold for the main header at 54–68px, Pretendard semibold for subheads at 22–28px, and a clean Korean serif such as Noto Serif KR or Nanum Myeongjo for the secondary line if contrast is needed.
- Color palette: company BI colors interpreted as white #FFFFFF, warm coral #F47C6B, mustard #D9A441, soft beige #F5F0E8, charcoal #222222, and pale gray #D9DDE3; adapt accents through {컬러 톤} while keeping the corporate palette coherent.
- Border/shadow: thin divider lines in pale gray, soft drop shadow 0px 8px 20px at 12% opacity for the hero element, subtle paper-edge shadows, and lightly layered cards that feel printed rather than glossy.
- Graphic system: use {타이포} to guide the Korean type personality; include rounded rectangles, small numbered chips, timeline dots, document tabs, checklist ticks, and small metadata labels that support onboarding content.
- Ratio handling: honor {비율} as a vertical cover ratio, with all text readable at 1024x1536 and the overall design feeling like a real corporate PDF cover or printed handbook.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: if using a portrait, use an 85mm f/1.8 look with shallow depth of field; if using product-style composition, use a 50mm standard lens with a clean frontal editorial framing.
- Lighting: soft diffused studio light from upper-left at 45°, gentle fill from right, low-contrast and office-friendly, with realistic paper texture and soft contact shadows.
- Color grade: warm white + coral + mustard with restrained neutral grays, slightly desaturated like a polished corporate handbook or modern SaaS onboarding deck.
- Material realism: visible matte paper grain, crisp ink edges, slight depth between cards/tabs, and a believable internal-document finish rather than a sterile mockup.

[6. MOOD]
Modern internal handbook cover — polished Naver/Kakao/Toss-style onboarding document, trustworthy and welcoming with a clean editorial system, enriched with realistic HR-guide metadata, quick-start cues, and warm first-day office details.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: "WELCOME ABOARD — 박서윤님, 합류를 환영합니다" must appear exactly as written in the headline.
- Korean text accuracy: W1 회사·문화 / W2 도구·계정 / W3 첫 프로젝트 / W4 1on1 must appear exactly and be clearly readable.
- Korean text accuracy: include readable supporting Korean strings such as "첫 주 체크리스트", "사내 포털 바로가기", "담당: People Team", "2026년 5월 업데이트", and "신입 OJT·온보딩 가이드" with correct Korean characters.
- Korean text accuracy: 신입 OJT·온보딩 가이드 표지 must be visually implied by the cover context, with all Korean characters rendered correctly.
- Layout invariant: cover must remain a vertical A4-style document with a clear title hierarchy, centered hero region, and four-part onboarding scope.
- Typography invariant: preserve crisp corporate document typography, not playful hand lettering.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites / unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
B2B business proposal / planning document cover, A4 vertical layout, premium consulting-firm tone for client-facing presentation.
Designed to read like a real printed strategy proposal cover with credible metadata, document-control details, and a polished executive presentation feel.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main title block: {제안서 제목} placed in the upper-left to upper-center zone, occupying about 22% of the height with clear hierarchy and confident corporate typography.
- Recipient line: {대상} positioned directly beneath the title in smaller type, aligned left, with a formal label such as “Prepared for”.
- Sender line: {제안사} placed below the recipient line, slightly lighter weight, paired with a formal label such as “Prepared by”.
- Hero visual zone: {대표 비주얼} anchored in the central-right or full-middle field depending on the visual type, treated as a restrained editorial business graphic with realistic depth, printed texture, and contextual detail.
- Color system: {컬러 톤} applied across background, accent rules, section tabs, small data cards, and graphic shapes with disciplined contrast.
- Document details: add realistic proposal-cover elements such as “CONFIDENTIAL”, “PROJECT PROPOSAL”, “DOC-ID: BP-2026-05-001”, “Revision 02”, “Executive Summary / Market Analysis / Implementation Roadmap”, and a small Korean label “대외비 · 제출용”.
- Footer zone: {버전·날짜} and {비율} placed at the bottom with document metadata styling, including a thin folio rule, page label “Cover”, and small contact text like “strategy office · proposal@company.co.kr”.
- Overall spacing: use a strong grid, professional alignment, and a realistic amount of cover information so it feels like an actual B2B proposal document rather than a blank mockup.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1) Header area (top 20%): set {제안서 제목} as the visual anchor in large type, with {대상} and {제안사} stacked underneath in a formal proposal cover layout. Add a small eyebrow line above the title such as “PROJECT PROPOSAL 2026” and a compact status tag “CONFIDENTIAL”.
2) Middle visual area (45–55%): render {대표 비주얼} as the central communication device, using either a monochrome city or office-district image with restrained color accent geometry, an infographic dashboard, a strategic roadmap diagram, or an abstract network pattern that feels corporate and decision-oriented.
3) Realistic supporting details: include 2–3 small business-content modules around the hero visual, such as KPI cards labeled “시장성”, “실행계획”, “ROI”, a thin timeline strip marked “Phase 01 / Phase 02 / Phase 03”, and tiny chart ticks or map-grid coordinates.
4) Background treatment: use a premium printed surface such as matte off-white, deep navy, charcoal, warm gray, or a subdued tinted field that supports the {컬러 톤}; add subtle paper grain, faint grid lines, and light ink layering for a believable physical proposal cover.
5) Accent system: introduce geometric blocks, thin rules, data-line motifs, corner markers, and chart-like overlays in the accent color, placed with precise alignment and clear hierarchy.
6) Footer area (bottom 10–12%): place {버전·날짜} and {비율} as small metadata, separated by a thin rule, alongside “문서번호 BP-2026-05-001”, “담당: 전략컨설팅본부”, and “Cover / 00”.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: use Pretendard or Noto Sans KR for clean corporate sans-serif headers, and Nanum Myeongjo or a refined Korean serif for a more formal editorial option; title weight 700–800, body/meta weight 400–500, with sizes that clearly establish hierarchy.
- Color palette: {컬러 톤} should resolve into specific tones such as deep navy #0E1B2E, gold accent #C9A24E, charcoal #2B2F36, warm gray #E7E2D8, forest green #2F5D50, or burgundy #6E2432.
- Print realism: show slight paper fiber, crisp ink edges, subtle tonal variation, realistic registration of thin rules, and a faint cover-stock texture suitable for a premium printed proposal.
- Border/shadow: use subtle dividers, hairline rules, corner registration marks, and soft flat shadows only if needed; if any shadow is used, keep it to a 4px y-offset, 12px blur, 15% opacity for a print-like, non-3D finish.
- Information design: charts, labels, and metadata must look purposeful and legible, like a consulting deck cover prepared for an executive client review.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: if a city or architectural image is used, shoot like a Canon EOS R5 with an RF 50mm f/1.2 lens set to f/5.6, editorial architectural framing, straight verticals, and crisp mid-distance detail; if the layout is graphic-first, treat it like a premium printed proposal photographed or rendered straight-on with precise flat-plan alignment.
- Lighting: use overcast diffused daylight for city imagery, or studio-soft even illumination for the document surface; maintain controlled contrast, readable typography, and gentle reflections on any printed ink.
- Color grade: muted corporate grade with deep navy, graphite, warm gray, and a restrained gold or single-accent overlay; keep saturation low, edges clean, and printed elements tactile.
- Rendering quality: high-resolution A4 cover look, sharp Korean text, realistic ink density, refined grid construction, and polished executive-document presentation.

[6. MOOD]
Premium consulting proposal cover — BCG / Accenture / Deloitte deck aesthetic with a realistic Korean B2B proposal-document finish, executive, confidential, strategic, and trustworthy.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: 반드시 정확히 보여야 하는 문자열:
  - {제안서 제목}
  - {대상}
  - {제안사}
  - {버전·날짜}
  - {비율}
- Additional Korean cover text must be clean and readable if included: “대외비 · 제출용”, “담당: 전략컨설팅본부”, “시장성”, “실행계획”, “ROI”, “문서번호”.
- Layout invariants: maintain a formal B2B proposal cover structure with strong hierarchy, executive metadata, document-control details, and a calm, trustworthy corporate feel.
- The hero visual must stay restrained and professional, supporting the proposal theme rather than becoming a flashy advertisement composition.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters
- Celebrity composites or unauthorized likeness

[1. PURPOSE]
Corporate PPT cover slide for a consulting-firm / tech-conference style deck, designed to open with immediate credibility, executive-level clarity, and believable real-world presentation detail.
Wide-format presentation cover with a strong typographic hierarchy, polished boardroom finish, and practical deck metadata such as date, version label, internal-use tag, footer navigation, and small topic indicators.

[2. OBJECT & COMPOSITION]
- Main title zone: {제목} set large and dominant, occupying the upper-left or left-center 38–45% of the frame with confident spacing and a clear executive reading path.
- Subtitle zone: {부제} positioned directly beneath the title as a smaller supporting line, aligned to the same left edge with tight but readable spacing.
- Presenter info: {발표자} placed as a clean metadata line near the subtitle or lower-left footer area, kept understated and professional.
- Visual treatment: {비주얼 결} should define the full-slide structure, using either a left abstract data/strategy graphic field with right-aligned text, or a top full-bleed editorial photo with a grounded lower text box.
- Realistic deck details: add small cover-slide elements such as “VOL.413”, “2026.05.01”, “Executive Briefing Deck”, “내부 검토용”, a small page marker “01”, and three compact agenda chips reading “시장 진단”, “전략 방향”, “실행 로드맵”. These should feel like authentic conference or consulting-deck cover metadata.
- Background treatment: premium corporate surface with subtle tactile grain, refined gradient, glass-panel overlay, faint grid coordinates, data-map lines, or soft architectural/photo texture depending on {비주얼 결}.
- Layout direction: keep all content aligned to a disciplined grid, with deliberate margins, balanced asymmetry, and a presentation cover hierarchy that feels intentional, expensive, and ready for a real executive meeting.

[3. CORE STRUCTURE]
1. Hero composition: place {비주얼 결} as the primary structural decision, establishing either a graphic-led cover or a photo-led cover while keeping the title instantly readable.
2. Title block: render {제목} in the largest typographic scale, with firm weight and crisp spacing so it reads as the sole focal point from a distance.
3. Subtitle support: place {부제} below the title in a smaller size, keeping it concise, balanced, and visually tethered to the headline.
4. Presenter metadata: add {발표자} as a restrained footer or side-note line, using small text and light contrast so it supports rather than competes.
5. Deck metadata layer: include a top or side micro-navigation system with “VOL.413”, “2026.05.01”, “Executive Briefing Deck”, and “내부 검토용”; add a small footer page indicator “01” and a thin progress rule to make the slide feel like part of a complete professional deck.
6. Topic indicators: add three small label chips or capsule tags reading “시장 진단”, “전략 방향”, “실행 로드맵”, placed near the lower edge, right rail, or under the subtitle without competing with the title.
7. Color execution: apply {컬러 톤} across the cover, using the accent color sparingly for emphasis, dividers, metadata labels, and small graphic details.
8. Typography system: apply {타이포} with clear hierarchy between title, subtitle, metadata, footer labels, and agenda chips, ensuring the slide feels like a premium consulting deck rather than a casual poster.
9. Format alignment: maintain {비율} as a strict widescreen presentation cover with balanced asymmetry and confident slide architecture.

[4. STYLE RULES]
- Typography: Pretendard for title and body, Bold/ExtraBold for the main headline, Medium or Regular for subtitle and presenter info; title around 72–90 pt, subtitle around 22–28 pt, metadata around 14–18 pt, micro labels around 9–12 pt.
- Color palette: use {컬러 톤} as the governing palette; if navy/white/gold is chosen, keep the base deep navy #0B1F3A, white #F7F7F5, and metallic gold #C8A96A; if alternative tones are chosen, preserve the same high-contrast corporate discipline.
- Cover assets: add refined presentation details such as thin divider rules, micro grid marks, small numeric labels, translucent panels, subtle chart fragments, abstract connection nodes, or a cropped business/technology photograph that supports the strategic theme.
- Panel and depth treatment: if a panel is used, apply a subtle 1px divider or a soft shadow with 4px y-offset, 10px blur, 12% opacity; glass or paper textures should look premium and restrained.
- Text density: metadata and agenda chips should enrich realism while staying secondary to {제목}; avoid turning the cover into a dense report page.

[5. VISUAL STYLE]
- Camera / lens: if using a photo-led cover, use a 50mm or 85mm lens look with controlled perspective, clean editorial framing, and no exaggerated distortion; if abstract-led, render as a high-end motion-graphics still with crisp vector precision.
- Lighting: studio-grade, even illumination; for photo-led layouts use softbox key light from upper-left at about 45° with gentle fill from the opposite side, preserving shadow detail and readability.
- Color grade: deep navy, bright white, and restrained gold accent; keep saturation controlled, contrast moderate-high, and highlights clean for a corporate keynote finish.
- Material realism: incorporate believable surfaces such as matte presentation paper, frosted glass overlays, brushed metal accent lines, subtle display glow, or soft conference-room ambience when compatible with {비주얼 결}.
- Graphic realism: abstract data visuals should feel generated from business intelligence dashboards or strategy maps, with fine lines, nodes, small axis ticks, and numeric micro labels rather than flat empty shapes.

[6. MOOD]
McKinsey / BCG-style executive presentation cover — polished keynote opener with the disciplined clarity of a top-tier consulting deck, enriched with realistic deck metadata, boardroom texture, and credible tech-conference visual language.

[7. CRITICAL]
- Korean text accuracy: the following verbatim Korean strings must appear correctly in the rendered image:
  - {제목}
  - {부제}
  - {발표자}
  - 내부 검토용
  - 시장 진단
  - 전략 방향
  - 실행 로드맵
- Additional cover metadata should appear correctly where used: “VOL.413”, “2026.05.01”, “Executive Briefing Deck”, and “01”.
- Composition invariant: the slide must preserve a strong cover-slide hierarchy with one dominant title, one supporting subtitle, and one small presenter line.
- The overall look must feel like a consulting firm or tech conference opening slide: confident, polished, highly legible, and suitable for a real boardroom presentation.
- If the chosen visual split is left graphic + right text, keep the text block aligned cleanly and ensure metadata, dividers, and decorative data elements support readability.

[8. 🚫 PROHIBITED]
- Fake official seals / certifications
- Broken Korean characters / 한글 깨짐
